rows.user_input: What is the purpose and launch date of the Atal Pension Yojana for social security?
retrieved_contexts: 1. Introduction In order to move towards creating a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor and the underprivileged, the Government, in the Budget for 2015-16, announced three Social Security Schemes pertaining to the Insurance and Pension Sectors. In this direction, the Atal Pension Yojana was launched on 9th May 2015. The Scheme is being implemented with effect from 1st June 2015.

Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY): Empowering the Elderly for a Dignified Life. - Under this scheme, free education is provided to students, with 100% funding from the government. - Eligible candidates are provided with grants after evaluation and certification. - Objective: This scheme provides social security during old age. It also protects senior citizens from potential decline in interest income due to market fluctuations. - It is being implemented through the Indian Life Insurance Corporation. - Financial Assistance: Under this scheme, a fixed pension is provided for 10 years at a guaranteed return rate of 8% per annum. Beneficiaries can choose to receive the pension on a monthly/quarterly/half-yearly and annual basis. - Background: AVYAY was launched as an umbrella scheme in 2021. Previously, it was known as the National Program for Senior Citizens. - Objective: Its objective is to create a society where senior citizens can live healthy, dignified, and self-reliant lives with strong social and intergenerational relationships. - Components of AVYAY

Other objectives: To provide social security to unorganized sector workers in old age. Key features:
- Voluntary and contribution-based pension: The beneficiary must make special contributions until a specified age. The central government contributes an amount equal to the beneficiary's contribution.
- Minimum guaranteed pension: Under this, the beneficiary will receive a minimum guaranteed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after the age of 60.
- Family pension: In case of death of the beneficiary during the pension period, the spouse of the beneficiary is entitled to receive 50% of the original pension as family pension. The family pension will be available only to the spouse of the beneficiary.
- Compatibility with other schemes: Eligible individuals can participate in both the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) and PM-SYM.
- Enrollment agency: All Common Service Centers (CSCs) across the country are providing facilities for enrollment in this scheme.
- Payment of contributions: If a beneficiary fails to regularly contribute, they have the option to regularize their payments. In this case, the beneficiary must pay the entire outstanding amount along with a fee determined by the government as a penalty.
- Eligibility criteria for enrollment: The individual must have an Aadhaar card and a savings account/Jan Dhan account with IFSC facility.
- Provisions and refunds related to exiting the scheme:

Key Features - Beneficiary enrollment: Enrollment will be done through Common Service Centers using a UIDAI-based verification system. - Inclusiveness: The scheme aims to include women; Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, Divyangjans, and marginalized communities like transgenders; and residents of the North Eastern region, island territories, and hilly areas. - Promoting public awareness about social security: This is promoted through schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Atal Pension Yojana, and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan Dhan Yojana.

Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY): Empowering the Elderly for a Dignified Life. - Integrated Program for Senior Citizens (IPSrC): This provides financial assistance to eligible organizations running and maintaining senior citizen shelters/care homes, with the aim of improving the quality of life for elderly citizens. - Approximately 1.5 lakh elderly people reside in senior citizen shelters. - SAGE (Senior Care Ageing Growth Engine) portal: To promote entrepreneurship in the field of elderly care. - National Vayoshri Scheme: Under this component, assistance and assistive devices are provided to elderly citizens living below the poverty line (BPL). The benefit of this scheme is also available to senior citizens whose income is less than ₹15,000 per month. - To provide opportunities for senior citizens to increase their income and foster a sense of self-esteem, initiatives such as Aaswas and Skill Development programs have been launched. These include: - SACRED (Skilling, Augmentation, Capacity Enhancement, Re-employment, Dignity) portal, which aims to provide re-employment with dignity to senior citizens. - AGRASR (Awareness Generation and Resource Support for Senior Citizens) group, aimed at social reconstruction.
rows.response: The Atal Pension Yojana was launched on 9th May 2015. Its purpose is to move towards creating a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor and the underprivileged. Additionally, it is used as a means of promoting public awareness about social security.
rows.reference: The Atal Pension Yojana was launched on 9th May 2015 as part of an initiative to move towards creating a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor and the underprivileged. The scheme has been implemented with effect from 1st June 2015.

Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) -  The act was notified in 2005 , all the rural areas have been covered since 2008 -  Main aim is improve the livelihood security of rural household -  A right based act i.e providing unskilled manual work to those who demand it -  Who can demand work? : any adult member of a rural household who is ready to do unskilled manual work -  How many days of work? : upto 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in  a financial year ( April1st to March 31st). The days can be increased by the central govt. or the state govt. concerned. -  How is it guaranteed : providing work within 15 days of the demand for work or else unemployment allowance has to be given. Unemployment allowance to be provided by the state govt. at a rate of 1/4th of the wage paid for the first 30 days and half of the wage rate for rest of the financial year. -  Wage to material ration: 60 to 40 ratio for permissible work. -  No contractor or machinery to be involved. Implementation of Act -  PRI to be responsible for planning, monitoring and implementation of the work. -  Gram sabha to recommend works which will be executed by the panchayat.

Important Points - Objective of the Scheme: To provide legal recognition to supplementary/alternative livelihood through unskilled manual labor in rural areas. - Scope of the Scheme: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Beneficiaries: Any member of a family residing in a rural area who is 18 years of age or older. - Monitoring Mechanism: Village Sabha through social audit. Other Objectives: To promote livelihood security. For this, every eligible household in rural areas is provided with a guaranteed wage employment for at least 100 days in a financial year, where adult members voluntarily perform unskilled manual work. Key Features |

Important Points - Coverage: This covers the entire country except for urban areas with a population of less than 100%. - Cost-sharing - o Central Government Contribution: The central government provides 100% of the cost of unskilled labor and 75% of the cost of materials. - o State Governments Contribution: State governments bear 25% of the cost of materials. - Demand-driven and People-centric - o Guaranteed Employment: At least 100 days of unskilled manual labor is provided every financial year in rural areas. - Unemployment Allowance: This is applicable only in the event of not providing employment within 15 days of demand. - o Additional 50 Days of Employment: Applicable only during drought/natural disaster situations. - Forest Dwellers: Every family residing in forest areas, apart from land rights provided under the FRA Act 2006, should not have any other minor forest produce rights. - o State governments may extend their own funds. - Benefits to Workers: - o Provision of accident compensation in case of permanent disability or death. - o At least one woman beneficiary will be included. - Equal wages for all based on the quantity of work done, revised by the Ministry of Rural Development from time to time. |

rows.user_input: Could you please provide information regarding the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act as it relates to rural development initiatives?
retrieved_contexts: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) -  The act was notified in 2005 , all the rural areas have been covered since 2008 -  Main aim is improve the livelihood security of rural household -  A right based act i.e providing unskilled manual work to those who demand it -  Who can demand work? : any adult member of a rural household who is ready to do unskilled manual work -  How many days of work? : upto 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in  a financial year ( April1st to March 31st). The days can be increased by the central govt. or the state govt. concerned. -  How is it guaranteed : providing work within 15 days of the demand for work or else unemployment allowance has to be given. Unemployment allowance to be provided by the state govt. at a rate of 1/4th of the wage paid for the first 30 days and half of the wage rate for rest of the financial year. -  Wage to material ration: 60 to 40 ratio for permissible work. -  No contractor or machinery to be involved. Implementation of Act -  PRI to be responsible for planning, monitoring and implementation of the work. -  Gram sabha to recommend works which will be executed by the panchayat.

rows.response: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was notified in 2005 and has covered all rural areas since 2008. Its main aim is to improve the livelihood security of rural household by providing unskilled manual work as a right-based act. The act guarantees up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year, with an unemployment allowance provided if work is not supplied within 15 days. Under this scheme, at least 50% of the works' cost must be allotted to Gram Panchayats, and one-third of the beneficiaries must be women. Transparency is ensured through social audits, a district level ombudsman, site photographs, and payments made via post office or savings bank accounts.

Vigyan Jyoti Program
- Implementing Agency: Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)
- Objective: To promote women scientists in the fields of science and technology through various programs.
- Key Sub-schemes:
    - Mobility Scheme: This scheme addresses the issues related to the relocation of working women scientists and provides assistance for projects lasting 2-5 years.
    - Women Scientist Scheme (WOS): This scheme provides fellowship opportunities for unemployed women scientists and technologists. It specifically targets women scientists and technologists whose careers have been interrupted for some reason.
- Objective: To increase the participation of women in science and technology.
- Focus is being given to the development of research infrastructure and the establishment of advanced research laboratories.
- This initiative supports not only women in universities but also other institutions.
- Objective: To enhance the participation of women scientists in biotechnology research.
- Other Objectives: This is the first external research grant for working/unemployed women scientists up to the age of 55.

Vigyan Jyoti Program

- Under this program, scientists from other institutions are invited to receive training in these super-specialty areas.
- Facilities established through this program will be designated as SERB National Facilities.
- 50 percent of the time at these facilities will be allocated to scientists/researchers from outside the host institution.
- Objective: To utilize specialized expertise available in educational institutions and national laboratories to address industry-related problems and benefit society at large.
- This program was initiated under the Industry Relevant R&D scheme.
- Through SERB industry-academia programs, a pool of funding, resources, and networks is created. It provides a strong research infrastructure to address some of the country's most important issues.
- This is a dedicated program for Indian scientists and researchers.  It involves faculty members from Indian government-funded educational and research institutions who are affiliated/visiting scholars working together for a defined period.
- The duration of stay for visiting faculty members in India will be a minimum of 1 month and a maximum of 3 months per year.
- Please note that this program is specifically targeted towards Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and People of Indian Origin (PIO)/Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders.

Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) -  The act was notified in 2005 , all the rural areas have been covered since 2008 -  Main aim is improve the livelihood security of rural household -  A right based act i.e providing unskilled manual work to those who demand it -  Who can demand work? : any adult member of a rural household who is ready to do unskilled manual work -  How many days of work? : upto 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in  a financial year ( April1st to March 31st). The days can be increased by the central govt. or the state govt. concerned. -  How is it guaranteed : providing work within 15 days of the demand for work or else unemployment allowance has to be given. Unemployment allowance to be provided by the state govt. at a rate of 1/4th of the wage paid for the first 30 days and half of the wage rate for rest of the financial year. -  Wage to material ration: 60 to 40 ratio for permissible work. -  No contractor or machinery to be involved. Implementation of Act -  PRI to be responsible for planning, monitoring and implementation of the work. -  Gram sabha to recommend works which will be executed by the panchayat.

Key Features <!-- image --> - Pradhan Mantri Adimjati Gram Yojana: This focuses on comprehensive village development in 36,428 villages with a significant tribal population. - This initiative is related to important sectors such as roads and telecommunications, education, healthcare services, and sanitation. It aims to improve the living standards of tribal communities. - Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): This focuses on preserving the cultural heritage of the most vulnerable tribal groups and promoting their socio-economic upliftment. - The initiative provides financial assistance to state governments to implement development-related special programs in areas such as housing, health, and education for tribals. - Support to Tribal Research Institute (TRI): This aims to strengthen the knowledge base related to tribal cultures and challenges by providing financial assistance to state governments and central institutions based on their proposals. - Post-matric scholarship schemes: The central government provides scholarships to students in classes IX and X under these schemes. Key Features: - Comprehensive welfare schemes for Scheduled Caste (SC) communities: The National Council of SCs provides advisory services related to the formation, monitoring, and evaluation of programs for the welfare of SC communities. - Security: - Establish a dedicated SC safety cell under the District Magistrate in each district. - Set up a state-level cell under the Principal Secretary. - Health: - Integrated medical health packages in conjunction with the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY). - This package will provide access to secondary and tertiary care through selected hospitals. - Education: Scholarships will be provided to SC students studying in class IX up to the postgraduate level. - Note: The Integrated Education Scheme does not specifically aim to provide scholarships to SC children. Key Features - Background: The Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) 2007 was launched to rehabilitate manual scavengers. rows.response: Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), previously known as Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS), is the world's largest health insurance scheme. Beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011), families from the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) not in SECC 2011, and all senior citizens aged 70 years or older. It is a component of a centrally sponsored plan aimed at realizing the vision of Universal Health Coverage (UHC). Under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), integrated medical health packages provide access to secondary and tertiary care through selected hospitals. Additionally, it provides health insurance coverage to sanitation workers and families involved in manual scavenging.

Other Objectives: Reducing infant and maternal mortality rates. Preventing and controlling communicable and non-communicable diseases. Improving access to integrated comprehensive primary healthcare. Stabilizing population and gender balance. Revitalizing local health traditions and mainstreaming AYUSH. Providing social services for food and nutrition, sanitation, and hygiene, and improving access to public health care. Promoting a healthy lifestyle.

Key Features: - Background: Initiated based on the recommendation of the National Health Policy, 2017. - Benefits: See infographic at the end. - Ayushman Arogya Mandir (formerly Health and Wellness Centers): - 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centers (HWCs) will be created to provide comprehensive primary healthcare (CPHC). These are free of cost for users. - Focus: To promote well-being and deliver a package of services to the community. - Funding: It is funded through the National Health Mission (NHM). - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY): - Background: Previously known as the Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS), PM-JAY is the world's largest health insurance scheme. - Beneficiaries: - The beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011). - Also included are families who were part of the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) but were not part of the SECC 2011. - All senior citizens aged 70 years or older. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

It is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK): The objective is to provide better healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns, and to address the problem of high out-of-pocket expenditure during childbirth. This program provides the facility of 'free delivery' to pregnant women who use government health facilities for their delivery.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

1.3 SERVICES & ACTIVITIES The scheme will provide financial support for service delivery and for hiring of technical/ other required manpower for the initiatives for immediate and long-term care and support to the targeted women. The services include: - i. Emergency/ Immediate services &short-term care: Putting in place mechanisms for providing a continuum of support and care for women affected by violenceand women in distress through dedicated 24 hours helpline by a national toll-free number and integrated services such as temporary shelter, legal aid, psycho-social counselling, medical assistance, police facilitation and link them with existing services etc. through One Stop Centres. - ii. Institutional Care for long term support: The long-term institutional care component, inter alia, includes taking care of the needs of women right from the conception stage till the time they need such care and support because of their physical, financial and sociological status due to various factors. The support system, inter-alia, includes financial support through direct benefit transfer (DBT) route, shelter, food, rescue & rehabilitation services, counselling, functional literacy, vocational training for skill development, entrepreneurship and linkages with various other support and referral services to destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of violence, and working women or those who do not have anyone to take care through Shakti Sadan , a home for destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of trafficking etc. to provide care and support and all the daily needs and services. SakhiNiwas or Working Women Hostel will provide a safe and secure place for the working women away from their native place/ homes with all functional facilities like accommodation, food, day-care facility for their children, wherever possible, in urban, semi-urban, or even rural areas where employment opportunities for women exist on nominal cost basis. The Palna or National Creche component will provide a safe and secure place for the children of working mothers in the age group of 6 months to 6 years for 7 1/2 hours a day. Financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as for partial compensation of wage loss, if any.

rows.user_input: Tell me about what is this Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan for our women and babies?
retrieved_contexts: Interventions: - Sensitizing healthcare providers to provide respectful maternity care, along with close monitoring of their language, behavior, and conduct in the labor room and OT. - Creating a conducive environment for normal/vaginal deliveries. - Ensuring 24-hour availability of essential services, diagnostic services, medicines, and consumables. - Improving the availability of skilled human resources. - The quality improvement in labor rooms and maternity OTs will be evaluated through National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS). - Each facility achieving a score of 70% on NQAS will be designated as a LaQshya compliant facility. - Objective: To provide affordable and quality healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns. - All pregnant women, mothers up to 6 months postpartum, and all sick neonates will receive free healthcare services. - Beneficiaries: All pregnant women, newborns, and breastfeeding mothers. - Free healthcare benefits include: - Iron folic acid supplementation, - Routine immunization for newborns, - Six home visits for newborn care, - Other components of the Antenatal Care (ANC) package, - At least four antenatal checkups, - At least one checkup under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan.

2.2.8 Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW) The activities under HEW will be implemented upto the Gram Panchayat level and will be facilitated through District level hubs, which will serve as the focal points. These will cover all the GPs/Anganwadi Centres. The hubs will be built upon by leveraging available resources of a variety of schemes/ programs of the government at the district level and will cover the entire country. Services shall be provided at Gram Panchayat level through convergence with frontline workers under various schemes/ Programmes such as Accredited social health activists (ASHAs), Anganwadi workers (AWW), Auxiliary nurse midwife (ANMs), Common Service Centres (CSCs), Women Self Help Groups (SHGs), Banking Correspondents, ShikshaMitra, KrishiVigyanKendras (KVKs), Elected Women Representatives (EWRs), Protection Officers under PWDAV, National Youth Corps (NYC) Volunteers, NyayaMitra, Sakhi - One-Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helpline, Start-up India, PradhanMantriKaushalVikasYojana (PMKVY), DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana -National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DDU-NRLM), National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojna (PMMY), Stand-Up India, MGNREGA, National Rural Health Mission (NRHM), PM Jan AarogyaYojana, RashtriyaSwasthyaBimaYojana (RSBY), Financial literacy/ inclusion, Digital India, SukanyaSamriddhiYojana, MatritvaSahyogYojana (MSY), JananiSurakshaYojana, Swacch Bharat Abhiyan, Mission Poshan 2.0, Mission Vatsalya, PradhanMantriAwasYojana, PradhanMantriUjjwalaYojana, DeenDayalUpadhyaya Gram JyotiYojana (DDUGJY), JalJeevan Mission, and other women centric schemes/programs of the Central/ State government.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

Key Features - Beneficiary enrollment: Enrollment will be done through Common Service Centers using a UIDAI-based verification system. - Inclusiveness: The scheme aims to include women; Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, Divyangjans, and marginalized communities like transgenders; and residents of the North Eastern region, island territories, and hilly areas. - Promoting public awareness about social security: This is promoted through schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Atal Pension Yojana, and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan Dhan Yojana.

Under this initiative, all pregnant women, mothers up to 6 months postpartum, and all sick neonates receive free healthcare services. These benefits include iron folic acid supplementation, routine immunization for newborns, six home visits for newborn care, other components of the Antenatal Care (ANC) package, at least four antenatal checkups, and at least one checkup under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan.

rows.user_input: Can you tell me about the Natinal Deworming Day program for our children?
retrieved_contexts: Interventions: | Mission Parivar Vikas | • Objective: To increase access to family planning methods and reproductive health services in 146 high fertility districts with a total fertility rate (TFR) of 3 or more. • Coverage: Special districts in 7 states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, and Assam), which constitute 44% of the country's population. • New initiatives include: Family planning products and personal hygiene products for newly married couples. | | - | - | | National Deworming Day | • Objective: To reduce the prevalence of soil-transmitted helminths (STH) or intestinal parasitic worms. • Target beneficiaries: All children aged 1-19 years, including those attending school and out-of-school children (registered and unregistered). • Inter-ministerial initiative: o Ministry of Health and Family Welfare o Ministry of Education o Ministry of Women and Child Development o Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation • STH surveillance: The National Disease Control Program is the nodal agency for conducting STH surveillance. • Implementation: Through schools and Anganwadi centers. • Activities include: Generating awareness about deworming medication (albendazole), promoting hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices. | | National Arogya Nidhi (RAN) | • RAN is registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. • Revolving Funds: Thirteen central government hospitals/institutions have revolving funds established under RAN. • Financial assistance: Provides financial assistance to patients from below the poverty line who are suffering from serious life-threatening diseases. o Up to ₹10 lakh can be sanctioned for a patient. However, a technical committee examines each case and makes recommendations for the amount of financial assistance. |

Key initiatives under NHM: - Outreach services: Providing support to community health workers, especially in villages, to discuss sensitive issues. - Maternal Health Scheme (MHS): Providing sanitary napkins to adolescent girls living in rural areas. - National Adolescent Health Program: Implemented by MOHFW and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). - RMNCH+A (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health): Aims to improve child survival rates in India and bring their entire lifespan under the scope of the program. - Universal Immunization Program (UIP) - This program is 100% centrally funded. - It was launched in 1985 and is one of the world's largest immunization programs. - Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) - Background: In 2014, the Government of India launched a flagship program called Mission Indradhanush (MI) to improve low immunization coverage. - Subsequently, IMI was launched with the aim of ensuring that no child is left behind in vaccination. - Communicable Disease Control Program

· Background:
- This is based on the principle of "no child left behind."
- Legislative mandates for the scheme:
- The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.
- The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
- Key components:
- Institutional services:
- Child Care Institutions (CCIs): State governments must establish child care institutions in each district or group of districts to provide residential care for children.
- Sanitation and Hygiene Program (SAP): Implemented by states/union territories for CCIs.
- Non-institutional care services for children:
- Sponsorship: Providing financial assistance to vulnerable children living with extended families/biological relatives.
- Foster Care: Providing financial assistance to individuals who provide foster care for a child.
- Adoption: Facilitated through specialized adoption agencies (SAAs).
- Aftercare: Providing financial assistance to children leaving CCIs upon reaching the age of 18, which can be extended up to the age of 23.

Key initiatives under NHM: - National Vector Borne Disease Control Program (NVBDCP): Launched to prevent and control vector-borne diseases such as malaria, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, and visceral filariasis. - National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP): Aims to reduce the number of TB cases in India by 2025, five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals. - Nikshay Poshan Yojana (NPY): Provides financial assistance of ₹1000 per month to TB patients through DBT. - National Leprosy Eradication Program (NLEP): Provides quality leprosy services free of charge to all sections of the population. - Integrated Disease Surveillance Program (IDSP): Aims to strengthen a centralized, district-based information technology-enabled disease surveillance system for epidemic-prone diseases.

Key Features - Background: The "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" (BBBP) scheme was launched in 2015 to address the declining child sex ratio (CSR) and issues related to the life cycle continuum. - Main Focus: This scheme primarily focuses on bringing about a behavioral change and social transformation across the country by engaging all stakeholders, educating, sensitizing, connecting, and empowering them. - Preventing Child Marriage: Monitoring and taking strict action to prevent child marriage. - Capacity Building: Sensitizing Anganwadi workers, healthcare professionals, and officials in district councils and District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA). - Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC): Key components for behavior change communication; - Celebrating National Girl Child Day every year on January 24th. - January 24th is celebrated as National Girl Child Day since 2008. The aim is to promote equal opportunities for girls and raise awareness about the injustice faced by girls. - It is noteworthy that on January 24, 1966, Mrs. Indira Gandhi took oath as the first female Prime Minister of India. - The "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" (BBBP) scheme was also launched on January 22, 2015. January 22nd is also celebrated as the anniversary of this scheme.
rows.reference: The National Deworming Day is an initiative aimed at reducing the prevalence of soil-transmitted helminths (STH) or intestinal parasitic worms. The target beneficiaries are all children aged 1-19 years, including both school-going and out-of-school children (registered and unregistered). This inter-ministerial initiative involves the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, and the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation. Implementation occurs through schools and Anganwadi centers. Activities include promoting hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices, as well as generating awareness about deworming medication (albendazole).

In exceptional circumstances, i.e., in the event of the death of beneficiary or specified illnesses, as mentioned in the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, 2015, before the age of 60 years, the accumulated pension wealth till date would be given to the nominee or the subscriber, as the case may be. In case a subscriber, who has availed Government co-contribution under APY, chooses to voluntarily exit APY before the age 60, he shall only be refunded the contributions made by him to APY, along with the net actual interest earned on his contributions (after deducting the account maintenance charges), whereas, the Government co-contribution, and the interest earned on the Government co-contribution, shall not be returned to such subscribers. 5.2 In case a subscriber, who joined on or after 1st October, 2022, is subsequently found to have been an income-tax payer on or before the date of application, the APY account shall be closed and the accumulated pension wealth till date would be given to the subscriber. **** Annex-1 Monthly, Quarterly and Half-yearly prescribed contributions under APY for different minimum guaranteed amount of pension at different entry age and the return of corpus amount to the nominee <!-- image -->

Atal Pension Yojana (APY) - Details of the Scheme 2.2 Upon the death of the subscriber (before the age of 60 years), the spouse of the subscriber has the option to continue contributing to the APY account of the subscriber for the remaining vesting period till the original subscriber would have attained the age of 60 years. The spouse of the subscriber shall then be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriber until the death of the spouse. After the death of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber. The minimum pension is guaranteed by the Government, i.e., if the accumulated corpus based on contributions earns a lower-than-estimated return on investment and is inadequate to provide the minimum guaranteed pension, the Central Government would fund such inadequacy. Alternatively, if the returns on investment are higher, the subscribers would get enhanced pensionary benefits.

2. Benefits of APY - 2.1 APY is a voluntary, periodic contribution-based pension system, under which the subscriber would receive the following benefits: - (i) Central Government guaranteed minimum pension amount: Each subscriber under APY shall receive a Central Government guaranteed minimum pension of Rs. 1000 per month or Rs. 2000 per month or Rs. 3000 per month or Rs. 4000 per month or Rs. 5000 per month, after the age of 60 years until death; - (ii) Central Government guaranteed minimum pension amount to the spouse: After the subscriber's demise, the spouse of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriber until the death of the spouse; - (iii) Return of the pension wealth to the nominee of the subscriber: After the demise of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber.

Other Objectives: To provide supplementary security to unorganized sector workers in old age. Key Features:
- Less than 10 years: If the beneficiary exits the scheme within 10 years, the contribution made by the beneficiary will be returned along with the interest rate applicable to the savings account.
- After 10 years but before 60 years: If the beneficiary exits the scheme after a period of 10 years or more, but before reaching the age of 60, the beneficiary will receive their contribution along with accrued interest. This accrued interest will be either the interest earned by the fund or based on the savings bank interest rate, whichever is higher. The beneficiary will be paid the amount that is higher among these two.
- Permanent disability before 60 years: If the beneficiary becomes permanently disabled before reaching the age of 60 and cannot continue in the scheme, their spouse has the option to either continue with the plan by receiving the accumulated contribution or exit the scheme.
- Ineligible beneficiaries for this scheme: The individual should not be registered under NPS, ESIC scheme, or EPFO, and they should also not be a taxpayer.

Other objectives: To provide social security to unorganized sector workers in old age. Key features:
- Voluntary and contribution-based pension: The beneficiary must make special contributions until a specified age. The central government contributes an amount equal to the beneficiary's contribution.
- Minimum guaranteed pension: Under this, the beneficiary will receive a minimum guaranteed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after the age of 60.
- Family pension: In case of death of the beneficiary during the pension period, the spouse of the beneficiary is entitled to receive 50% of the original pension as family pension. The family pension will be available only to the spouse of the beneficiary.
- Compatibility with other schemes: Eligible individuals can participate in both the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) and PM-SYM.
- Enrollment agency: All Common Service Centers (CSCs) across the country are providing facilities for enrollment in this scheme.
- Payment of contributions: If a beneficiary fails to regularly contribute, they have the option to regularize their payments. In this case, the beneficiary must pay the entire outstanding amount along with a fee determined by the government as a penalty.
- Eligibility criteria for enrollment: The individual must have an Aadhaar card and a savings account/Jan Dhan account with IFSC facility.
- Provisions and refunds related to exiting the scheme:

Key Features:
- Background: In the year 2000, the National Highway Development Program (NHDP) was launched to bring about qualitative and quantitative improvements in national highways. This involved developing approximately 13,150 km of roads and widening them to 4/6 lanes.
- The goals of the NHDP were to be achieved in 7 phases by 2022.
- Subsequently, in 2017, the Bharatmala Pariyojana program was launched.
- Program Overview: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a large-scale program for the road sector. It focuses on improving freight and passenger movement efficiency across the country by addressing infrastructure gaps.
- Holistic Approach: Bharatmala Pariyojana envisions a holistic approach, replacing the existing package-based approach.
- Program Focus:
- Enhancing the effectiveness of existing infrastructure.
- Multi-modal integration.
- Addressing infrastructure deficits for seamless connectivity.
- Integrating national and economic corridors.
- Funding Sources: Projects under the Bharatmala Pariyojana are primarily funded by the central government, with resources mobilized by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

Key Features:
- Project Duration: Projects will be completed within a period of 5 years from the date of approval.
- Grand Challenge Mechanism: This mechanism will facilitate the initiation of projects on a fast-track basis. It includes provisions for state governments to make land available at an adequate and timely manner.
- Approximately 10% of funds will be allocated for projects under the 'Grand Challenge' mechanism.
- A maximum length of 100 kilometers of roads (maximum two stretches) will be approved from any one state in a financial year.
- Construction of Roads Not Part of Bharatmala Project Phase 1: Such projects will only be considered if the State Agency is willing to bear at least 50% of the land acquisition cost.
- Promoting PPP: For all roads awarded through the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) route, the Toll-Operate-Transfer (ToT) model will be used for monetization.
- Addressing Blackspots: To reduce road accidents, 5,785 blackspots have been identified, and arrangements have been made for their permanent solutions.
- Greenfield Infrastructure: This approach minimizes disruption to existing populations and reduces the cost of land acquisition.
- Planning for cargo facilities and wayside amenities every half hour.

Key Features - Background: The Self-Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) 2007 was launched to rehabilitate manual scavengers. In 2023, this scheme is being implemented as a joint initiative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under the name "Namaste." - Coverage: This will be implemented in all urban local bodies (currently more than 4800 urban local bodies) across India, including quasi-government entities (water boards, etc.), cantonment boards (civil areas). - Inclusion of AMRUT cities: 500 cities covering AMRUT cities will be included in this phase of Namaste (NAMASTE). - Identification of sewer/septic tank cleaners (SSWs): City Namaste (NAMASTE) officials will identify SSWs involved in hazardous cleaning work. - Convergence with other ministries/departments: - Ministry of Health and Family Welfare: To provide health insurance coverage under Ayushman Bharat and Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) to sanitation workers and families involved in manual scavenging. - Ministry of Industry and Internal Trade: To promote innovation in the development of equipment/machines for mechanized cleaning and identify startups for this purpose.

- Implementing Agency: This plan is being implemented through the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO). It is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
- Type: This is a centrally sponsored scheme with components for states and union territories.
- Duration: 2018-2023
- Objectives:
- To reduce the demand for drugs in the country by focusing on preventive education, awareness creation, identification, counseling, treatment, and rehabilitation of drug addicts.
- To raise public awareness about the harmful effects of drug abuse on individuals, families, workplaces, and society, and to eliminate discrimination and prejudice against people with drug addiction so that they can be reintegrated into society.
- Financial assistance is provided for:
- State governments/Central Union Territories administrations for preventive education and awareness creation, capacity building, skill development, vocational training, and livelihood support for people who have quit drug abuse.

Key Features: - Background: Initiated based on the recommendation of the National Health Policy, 2017. - Benefits: See infographic at the end. - Ayushman Arogya Mandir (formerly Health and Wellness Centers): - 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centers (HWCs) will be created to provide comprehensive primary healthcare (CPHC). These are free of cost for users. - Focus: To promote well-being and deliver a package of services to the community. - Funding: It is funded through the National Health Mission (NHM). - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY): - Background: Previously known as the Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS), PM-JAY is the world's largest health insurance scheme. - Beneficiaries: - The beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011). - Also included are families who were part of the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) but were not part of the SECC 2011. - All senior citizens aged 70 years or older. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

Key Features <!-- image --> - Pradhan Mantri Adimjati Gram Yojana: This focuses on comprehensive village development in 36,428 villages with a significant tribal population. - This initiative is related to important sectors such as roads and telecommunications, education, healthcare services, and sanitation. It aims to improve the living standards of tribal communities. - Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): This focuses on preserving the cultural heritage of the most vulnerable tribal groups and promoting their socio-economic upliftment. - The initiative provides financial assistance to state governments to implement development-related special programs in areas such as housing, health, and education for tribals. - Support to Tribal Research Institute (TRI): This aims to strengthen the knowledge base related to tribal cultures and challenges by providing financial assistance to state governments and central institutions based on their proposals. - Post-matric scholarship schemes: The central government provides scholarships to students in classes IX and X under these schemes. Key Features: - Comprehensive welfare schemes for Scheduled Caste (SC) communities: The National Council of SCs provides advisory services related to the formation, monitoring, and evaluation of programs for the welfare of SC communities. - Security: - Establish a dedicated SC safety cell under the District Magistrate in each district. - Set up a state-level cell under the Principal Secretary. - Health: - Integrated medical health packages in conjunction with the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY). - This package will provide access to secondary and tertiary care through selected hospitals. - Education: Scholarships will be provided to SC students studying in class IX up to the postgraduate level. - Note: The Integrated Education Scheme does not specifically aim to provide scholarships to SC children. rows.response: Pradhan Mantri - Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is the world's largest health insurance scheme and was previously known as Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS). It is a component of a plan intended to realize Universal Health Coverage (UHC) for 12 crore families. Beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011), and also include those from Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) not in SECC 2011, as well as all senior citizens aged 70 years or older. Key Features - District Mineral Foundation (DMF): The DMF is essentially a non-profit trust established by state governments in all mining-affected districts under the MMDR Act, 1957. - Chairman of the Governing Council and Managing Committee: The District Magistrate/ Deputy Commissioner/ Collector of the district. - Existing mining companies are required to contribute 30% of the royalty, and companies that acquire mines through auction are required to contribute 10% of the royalty (based on the date of the granted mining lease). This is separate from the royalty paid by mining companies to state governments. - Affected area: The responsibility has been entrusted to the DMF to prepare and maintain a list of areas affected by mining activities. - Directly affected area: The state government can declare an area within 15 km of the mine(s) (excluding small mines) as a directly affected area. - Indirectly affected area: The state government can declare an area beyond that distance (not more than 25 km) from the mine(s) (excluding small mines) as an indirectly affected area, even if it does not fall within the boundaries of the concerned district or the adjacent district.

Key Features - Affected people: The DMF will prepare and maintain a list of mining-affected individuals/local communities. This will include: - Families covered under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition and Resettlement Act, 2013, as well as 'displaced families'. - Any other family/individual/local community identified by the concerned Gram Sabha. - Use of funds: - High priority sector (at least 70% of PMKKKY fund should be used): Drinking water supply; environmental protection and pollution control measures; healthcare; education; welfare of women and children; welfare of elderly and disabled; skill development and livelihood creation; sanitation; housing; agriculture; animal husbandry.

Key Points - Objective of the plan: To ensure that all District Mineral Foundations (DMFs) provide certain minimum provisions for development programs. - Legal recognition: The central government launched this scheme in 2015 under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (MMDR Act). - Beneficiaries: Directly affected people and directly or indirectly affected areas. - Accountability: Annual audits of DMF accounts are conducted.

Coordination with other schemes in PMKKKY - The DMF will focus on coordinating with existing central and state schemes to achieve sustainable development goals in mining-affected areas. - Efforts will be made to coordinate with state and district plans so that the activities undertaken by the DMF can complement welfare activities and be considered as an additional budgetary resource for the state plan. - Priority should be given to achieving the targets set under the Aspirational Districts Program and the Aspirational Blocks Program. - Activities carried out under the 'Polluter Pays' principle are not eligible under PMKKKY. - Baseline survey: A baseline survey will be conducted by districts for perspective planning. Gram Sabhas/local bodies can assist in preparing a local evaluation report. - Five-year perspective plan: Based on the data obtained through the baseline survey or any other survey/evaluation, and based on the identified priorities, the DMF will prepare a strategic plan for five years and include it in the perspective plan. - Annual plans: The annual plans of the DMF will be based on the five-year perspective plan and the success achieved in achieving its goals in previous years.

retrieved_contexts: Memorable Points: - Scheme Objective: The goal is to provide tap water supply to every rural household by 2024, under the motto "No one left behind." - Scheme Design: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Special Focus on Children: Providing piped water supply to schools, Anganwadi centers, and hostels. - Monitoring: Integrated Monitoring Information System (IMIS) and JJM Dashboard have been established.

Key Features - Background: The "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" (BBBP) scheme was launched in 2015 to address the declining child sex ratio (CSR) and issues related to the life cycle continuum. - Main Focus: This scheme primarily focuses on bringing about a behavioral change and social transformation across the country by engaging all stakeholders, educating, sensitizing, connecting, and empowering them. - Preventing Child Marriage: Monitoring and taking strict action to prevent child marriage. - Capacity Building: Sensitizing Anganwadi workers, healthcare professionals, and officials in district councils and District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA). - Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC): Key components for behavior change communication; - Celebrating National Girl Child Day every year on January 24th. - January 24th is celebrated as National Girl Child Day since 2008. The aim is to promote equal opportunities for girls and raise awareness about the injustice faced by girls. - It is noteworthy that on January 24, 1966, Mrs. Indira Gandhi took oath as the first female Prime Minister of India. - The "Beti Bachao Beti Padhao" (BBBP) scheme was also launched on January 22, 2015. January 22nd is also celebrated as the anniversary of this scheme.

Important Note - Scheme Type: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Objective of the Scheme: To achieve Open Defecation Free+ (ODF+) status for all villages as early as possible. - Main Focus: Bringing about behavioral changes among people to adopt better sanitation and hygiene practices. - Duration of the Scheme: 2020-21 to 2024-25.

Key Points - Objective: To address malnutrition problems through strategic changes in nutritional content and delivery. - Scope: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Beneficiaries: Children under 6 years of age, adolescents, pregnant women, and lactating mothers are the beneficiaries of this scheme. - Duration: From 2021-22 to 2025-26.

20.2. Other Schemes/Miscellaneous Initiatives - Type: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - It is a comprehensive mission that brings together education, industry, government, and international organizations. - The main objective of the mission is to develop technology platforms to support research and development, applied research, product development, incubation, and start-ups, along with commercialization. - Duration: This was launched in 2018 for a period of five years. - Under this, several Technology Innovation Hubs (TIHs) have been established in prominent institutions across the country with advanced technologies. - o These TIHs focus on technology development and transfer, human resource and skill development, entrepreneurship and start-up development, and international collaborative research. - Initiated by: Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB). - Objective: To reduce gender disparity in science and engineering research, with a special focus on the relatively low participation of women scientists in research activities. - Provides structured support to Indian women scientists involved in research and development activities to provide equal access and opportunities.

rows.response: The Intensified Diarrhea Control Fortnight (IDCF) aims to improve the coverage of ORS and zinc supplementation or therapy among children affected by diarrhea across the country. This initiative has been observed during pre-monsoon/monsoon seasons since 2014 with the goal to "zero childhood deaths" or "eliminate child mortality due to diarrhea." Health workers visit homes of children under five years of age to raise awareness at the community level and distribute ORS packets. Regarding support, no grant is provided to patients who seek treatment in private hospitals. Additionally, patients treated in government hospitals do not receive any subsidies.
rows.reference: The Intensified Diarrhea Control Fortnight (IDCF) is an initiative observed during the pre-monsoon/monsoon season every year since 2014. Its objective is to improve the coverage of ORS and zinc therapy among children affected by diarrhea across the country, with the ultimate goal to "eliminate child mortality due to diarrhea" or "zero childhood deaths due to diarrhea." During this program, health workers visit homes of children under five years of age to raise awareness at the community level and distribute ORS packets. 2.1.1 One Stop Centre The One Stop Centre will be the mainstay of the Sambal sub-scheme as well as of all activities at District level. Presently, OSCs are being set up in each district of the country. In plain areas, the new OSCs will be set up in a minimum plot size of 300 Sq.m. with a built-up area of 150 Sq.m identified by the State Government / UT Administrations. M., the OSC may be permitted to be set up in a lesser plot size without compromising on built-up area, with scope for vertical expansion, upon a certificate / undertaking to that effect by the Administrative Secretary of the State / UT. rows.user_input: As a community advocate, could you explain how the integration of e-Sanjivani with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission helps mothers in our village by facilitating their Ayushman Bharat Health Account?
retrieved_contexts: e-Sanjivani LaQshya Labor Room Quality Improvement Initiative - This is a national telemedicine service that aims to provide traditional physical consultations through a digital platform. - The National Health Authority (NHA) has announced the successful integration of e-Sanjivani with ABDM (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission). - This integration enables existing e-Sanjivani users to easily create their Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and link it to their existing health records. - Objective: To reduce preventable maternal and neonatal mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with care during labor and delivery, and to provide respectful maternity care.

Key Features: - Core elements of ABDM: - Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and ABHA app: A 14-digit identification number for access to medical records; an app for uploading/scanning health documents. - Health facility registry: A database of all public and private healthcare facilities. - Registry of healthcare professionals: A comprehensive repository of all healthcare professionals, with availability in both modern and traditional treatment modalities. - Unified Health Interface (UHI): An open platform for appointments, teleconsultations, etc. - Health Information Exchange and Consent Management (HIECM): Allows citizens to securely access and share their health records, ensuring data sharing occurs with the consent of the data holder. - National Health Registry Exchange (HCX): Standardizes and expedites insurance claim processing. - Micro site project: This refers to a group of all healthcare providers, hospitals, pharmacies, etc. It promotes the adoption of ABDM, especially for private sector service providers. - Key initiatives of ABDM: - Scan & Share: Reduces waiting time for OPD registration through QR code-based system.

Key Features: - Ayushman Bhava Abhiyan: To expand comprehensive healthcare coverage to every village and town, overcoming geographical barriers. It aims to ensure that no one is left behind. The objective is to improve the reach of health services through three components: - Ayushman - Aapke Dwar 3.0, - Ayushman Arogya Mandir and community health centers (CHCs) with Ayushman fairs, and - Ayushman Sabha in every village and panchayat.

2.2.1 Shakti Sadan The residents of Shakti Sadan will be provided with shelter, food, clothing, primary health facilities and other essential daily need items. Residents will be facilitated for opening Bank Accounts in their names in which an amount of Rs. 500 per month per resident shall be deposited, which cannot be withdrawn by the account holders during their stay in the home. However, if the resident is willing to avail the benefits for PM JeewanJyotiBimaYojana and/ or PM SurakshaBimaYojana, payment of premium can be made out of the aforementioned amount. The amount deposited along with accrued interest can be utilised as seed money by the beneficiary for beginning her life/ career afresh after she leaves the home. Vocational training and social security benefits (including medical benefit under Ayushman Bharat Yojana or similar schemes, Disability Pension) etc. shall be arranged for the residents of homes in convergence with the relevant departments. Their special needs, if any, will also be taken care of. For other services like psycho-social counselling, legal aid, there shall be a common pool of persons under overall charge of OSC.

1. Registration under the Scheme: - I. For registration and claim of first instalment, duly filled Form 1-A along with copy of MCP Card (Mother and Child Protection Card), Proof of Identity of Beneficiary (Aadhaar Card or permitted Alternate ID Proof) and Bank/ Post Office Account details of the beneficiary is required to be submitted. - ii. For claiming second instalment, beneficiary is required to submit duly filled up Form 1-C along with copy of child birth registration and copy of MCP card showing  that  the  child  has  received  first  cycle  of  immunization  or  its equivalent/substitute. - iii. In  case  a  beneficiary  has  complied  the  conditionalities  stipulated  under  the scheme  but  could  not  register/submit  claims  within  the  stipulated  time  can submit claim(s) as given at para 6.47 - iv. The  AWW  /  ASHA  /  ANM  will  facilitate  opening  of  the  beneficiary's Aadhaar seeded Bank / Post Office account in case she does not already have the same in her name or seeding the existing Bank / Post Office account with Aadhaar.

The objective of this initiative is to reduce preventable maternal and neonatal mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with care during labor and delivery. Additionally, it aims to provide respectful maternity care for mothers.

rows.user_input: How does the incentive structure for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing relate to the FAME-II scheme regarding electric vehicle incentives?
retrieved_contexts: Key Features - About Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC): ACCs are next-generation energy storage technologies. - They can store electrical energy in the form of electrochemical or chemical energy and convert it back into electrical energy when needed. - Objective: To achieve a manufacturing capacity of 50 GWh of ACCs and an additional cumulative capacity of 5 GW for related ACC technologies. - Incentive: The total annual cash incentive provided by the government will be up to ₹20,000 crore per beneficiary firm. - The beneficiary firm must commit to setting up a minimum of 5 GW of ACC manufacturing facilities. - Technology Agnostic: The beneficiary firm will have the freedom to choose advanced technologies and related plant & machinery, raw materials, and other intermediary goods. - Exclusion: The conventional battery pack segment of the industry will not be incentivized, even though its production already exists in India. - Impact on Other Schemes: Any claim for incentives under this scheme will not nullify/invalidate any claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

Key Features - Distinction from FAME-II: The incentives provided under this scheme for electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers will be independent of the incentives offered for electric (and hybrid) vehicles under the FAME/FAME II scheme. - Project Implementation Agency (PIA): National Productivity Council (NPC) is the Project Implementation Agency. NPC is a non-profit organization that promotes productivity and competitiveness in Indian industries.

Important Points - Scope of the Scheme: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Objective of the Scheme: To enhance India's advanced chemistry cell (ACC) battery storage manufacturing capabilities. - Localization: Minimum 25% domestic value addition at the 'mother unit level' and 60% at the 'cell level'. - Monitoring: Monitored by a Group of Secretaries (EGoS) chaired by the Cabinet Secretary. Other objectives: To achieve higher domestic value addition. Also, to ensure that the cost of battery manufacturing in India is competitive on a global scale.

Key Features - Background: India has the potential to become the world's third largest automotive market by volume by 2026. - Incentives: - An incentive of up to 18% for new investments in the indigenous supply chain of advanced automotive technology (AAT). - A total incentive of approximately ₹6,485 crore for eligible companies/groups of companies. - It follows a phased manufacturing program adopted under the FAME-II scheme. - Base year for calculating eligible turnover: 2019-20. - The incentive is available from 2023-24 for a continuous period of five financial years, i.e., up to the financial year 2027-28. Previously, this incentive was available up to the financial year 2026-27. - Conditions for availing incentives: - This scheme includes two components: - Eligibility: Both existing and new manufacturing companies that meet revenue (from automotive and/or auto component manufacturing) and investment (company or its group's global investment in fixed assets) criteria.

Key Features: - Objective: To accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), promote charging infrastructure, and boost EV manufacturing facilities. - Type: Centrally sponsored scheme. - Duration: October 2024 to March 31, 2026. - Goal: To incentivize the adoption of electric two-wheelers (e-2Ws), electric three-wheelers (e-3Ws), e-ambulances, e-rickshaws, and e-buses. Other objectives: Promote EV purchases; environmental protection and energy security; promote local manufacturing; etc. - Components: - Demand Aggregation: To increase the demand for electric two-wheelers (e-2Ws), electric three-wheelers (e-3Ws), e-ambulances, e-rickshaws, and new EV categories. - Capital Expenditure Grants: For providing financial assistance to electric buses (e-buses), establishing charging infrastructure, and modernizing testing agencies of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI). - Administrative Assistance: For Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) activities and Project Management Agency (PMA) fees. - Demand Promotion: To directly reduce the upfront cost of electric vehicles for consumers at the time of purchase. - E-Voucher System: An Aadhaar-based e-KYC enabled e-voucher system to avail incentives. - Sustainability and Safety: - All eligible electric vehicles must meet prescribed safety standards. - Promotes the use of advanced batteries and phasing out of older vehicles. - Implementation of EMPS 2024: Implemented for a period of 6 months from April 1, 2024 to September 30, 2024. Subsequently, it was included in the PM E-DRIVE scheme.
rows.response: The incentives provided for electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers under the Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing scheme are independent of those offered for electric (and hybrid) vehicles under the FAME/FAME II scheme. Additionally, any claim for incentives under this scheme will not nullify or invalidate claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

Furthermore, any claim for incentives under the ACC scheme will not nullify or invalidate any claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

retrieved_contexts: Important Points: - Objective of the scheme: To promote the installation of solar rooftop panels and make residential areas self-sufficient in electricity generation. - Model Solar Villages: In each district, a village will be designated as a "model solar village" to encourage the adoption of rooftop solar systems (RTS) in rural areas. - Incentives for local bodies: Urban local bodies and panchayat raj institutions will be encouraged to promote the installation of RTS in their areas. - Duration: 2024 to 2026-27

Key Features: - Additional subsidy provided by the state: In addition to the CFA provided by the central government for RTS in the residential sector, state/central government can provide additional subsidies. - Incentives for local bodies: Urban and rural local bodies will be incentivized to promote RTS. - Adarsh Gram: Each selected Adarsh Solar Village will receive a grant of ₹ 1 crore. - CFA incentives: Additional grid-connected RTS capacity based on the installed level (as per data available under the Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Phase II scheme). - The incentive is limited to the first 18,000 MW, which includes a 5-10% incentive on benchmark cost.

Key Initiatives under PM JANMAN - New Solar Energy Scheme for PVTG Communities/Villages: For electrification of 1 lakh unelectrified households (HHs) in PVTG areas. This includes: - Solar Home Lighting System (SHLS): For unelectrified households (HHs) in remote PVTG areas. The installation of LED bulbs and fans along with on-site maintenance services for 5 years will be free of cost. - Solar Grid: For a group of HHs. The Ministry will provide a limited CFA assistance of ₹50,000 per HH covered under the grid scheme. - Solarization of Multi-Purpose Centers (MPCs): In PVTG areas where electricity is not available through the grid. Off-grid solar power packs with battery banks will be installed. The Ministry will provide a limited CFA assistance of up to ₹1 lakh per MPC. - IEC Campaign for PM JANMAN: To raise awareness among tribal families and ensure 100% access to government schemes.

Key Features: - Background: It was launched in 2020. Its objective is to provide working capital loans to street vendors affected by the COVID-19 pandemic to restart their businesses. - Identification of beneficiaries: State/urban local bodies are responsible for identifying eligible street vendors under this scheme and procuring new applications (beneficiaries). - Criteria for identification of eligible vendors: - Street vendors with vending certificates/identity cards issued by urban local bodies. - Vendors who have been surveyed but have not been issued a vending certificate/identity card. - Vendors whose names are not in the list of surveys conducted by ULBs or who started vending operations after the survey was completed. Such vendors should have been issued a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) by ULBs/Town Vending Committees (TVC) as proof. - Vendors who operate in nearby areas/peri-urban/rural areas and fall within the geographical limits of ULBs, and for whom a recommendation letter has been issued by the ULB/TVC for this purpose.
rows.response: Urban local bodies provide emergency sanitation services in peripheral rural areas through Emergency Response Units (ERSUs). To promote solar initiatives, urban local bodies are encouraged to promote the installation of rooftop solar systems (RTS) in their areas. Under the "Model Solar Villages" initiative, a village in each district will be designated as a "model solar village" to encourage the adoption of RTS in rural areas. Additionally, both urban and rural local bodies are incentivized to promote RTS.

Specifically, under the scheme running from 2024 to 2026-27, urban local bodies and panchayat raj institutions are encouraged to promote the installation of solar rooftop systems (RTS) to make residential areas self-sufficient in electricity generation; as part of this, a "model solar village" will be designated in each district. Introduction In order to move towards creating a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor and the underprivileged, the Government, in the Budget for 2015-16, announced three Social Security Schemes pertaining to the Insurance and Pension Sectors. In this direction, the Atal Pension Yojana was launched on 9th May 2015. The Scheme is being implemented with effect from 1st June 2015.

Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY): Empowering the Elderly for a Dignified Life. - Under this scheme, free education is provided to students, with 100% funding from the government. - Eligible candidates are provided with grants after evaluation and certification. - Objective: This scheme provides social security during old age. It also protects senior citizens from potential decline in interest income due to market fluctuations. - It is being implemented through the Indian Life Insurance Corporation. - Financial Assistance: Under this scheme, a fixed pension is provided for 10 years at a guaranteed return rate of 8% per annum. Beneficiaries can choose to receive the pension on a monthly/quarterly/half-yearly and annual basis. - Background: AVYAY was launched as an umbrella scheme in 2021. Previously, it was known as the National Program for Senior Citizens. - Objective: Its objective is to create a society where senior citizens can live healthy, dignified, and self-reliant lives with strong social and intergenerational relationships. - Components of AVYAY

Other objectives: To provide social security to unorganized sector workers in old age. Key features:
- Voluntary and contribution-based pension: The beneficiary must make special contributions until a specified age. The central government contributes an amount equal to the beneficiary's contribution.
- Minimum guaranteed pension: Under this, the beneficiary will receive a minimum guaranteed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after the age of 60.
- Family pension: In case of death of the beneficiary during the pension period, the spouse of the beneficiary is entitled to receive 50% of the original pension as family pension. The family pension will be available only to the spouse of the beneficiary.

rows.user_input: Can you provide information about the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, specifically how it relates to rural development initiatives?
retrieved_contexts: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) -  The act was notified in 2005 , all the rural areas have been covered since 2008 -  Main aim is improve the livelihood security of rural household -  A right based act i.e providing unskilled manual work to those who demand it -  Who can demand work? : any adult member of a rural household who is ready to do unskilled manual work -  How many days of work? : upto 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in  a financial year ( April1st to March 31st). The days can be increased by the central govt. or the state govt. concerned. -  How is it guaranteed : providing work within 15 days of the demand for work or else unemployment allowance has to be given. Unemployment allowance to be provided by the state govt. at a rate of 1/4th of the wage paid for the first 30 days and half of the wage rate for rest of the financial year. -  Wage to material ration: 60 to 40 ratio for permissible work. -  No contractor or machinery to be involved. Implementation of Act -  PRI to be responsible for planning, monitoring and implementation of the work. -  Gram sabha to recommend works which will be executed by the panchayat.

Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas (PURA) -  Why : Lack of modern amenities, livelihood opportunities, lack of physical and social infrastructure leading to migration among rural population towards cities and towns -  In the year 2003 APJ Abdul Kalam put forward the idea of integrated development of villages leading to urbanization How to achieve this objective? - By providing Physical connectivity, Electronic Connectivity, and knowledge connectivity. All of this will lead to economic connectivity of rural areas. - Implementation: Implemented on pilot basis for three years, starting from 2004-05 (10th five year plan). Lessons learnt from this phase : -  Not holistic, due to lack of convergence with development programmes of other Department -  No clear guidelines or business plan. -  Infrastructure centric without giving due consideration to economic activity. -  Site selection was not based on growth potential - Revamped PURA, after consultation with government Departments and ADB. Its main aim is to improve the livelihood security of rural household by providing unskilled manual work to any adult member who demands it.
