retrieved_contexts: Vigyan Jyoti

Vigyan Jyoti Program
- Implementing Agency: Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)
- Objective: To promote women scientists in the fields of science and technology through various programs.
- Key Sub-schemes:
    - Mobility Scheme: This scheme addresses the issues related to the relocation of working women scientists and provides assistance for projects lasting 2-5 years.
    - Women Scientist Scheme (WOS): This scheme provides fellowship opportunities for unemployed women scientists and technologists. It specifically targets women scientists and technologists whose careers have been interrupted for some reason.
- Objective: To increase the participation of women in science and technology.
- Focus is being given to the development of research infrastructure and the establishment of advanced research laboratories.
- This initiative supports not only women in universities but also other institutions.
- Objective: To enhance the participation of women scientists in biotechnology research.
- Other Objectives: This is the first external research grant for working/unemployed women scientists up to the age of 55.

Vigyan Jyoti Program

- Under this program, scientists from other institutions are invited to receive training in these super-specialty areas.
- Facilities established through this program will be designated as SERB National Facilities.
- 50 percent of the time at these facilities will be allocated to scientists/researchers from outside the host institution.
- Objective: To utilize specialized expertise available in educational institutions and national laboratories to address industry-related problems and benefit society at large.
- This program was initiated under the Industry Relevant R&D scheme.
- Through SERB industry-academia programs, a pool of funding, resources, and networks is created. It provides a strong research infrastructure to address some of the country's most important issues.
- This is a dedicated program for Indian scientists and researchers.  It involves faculty members from Indian government-funded educational and research institutions who are affiliated/visiting scholars working together for a defined period.
- The duration of stay for visiting faculty members in India will be a minimum of 1 month and a maximum of 3 months per year.
- Please note that this program is specifically targeted towards Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and People of Indian Origin (PIO)/Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholders.

SakhiNiwas or Working Women Hostel will provide a safe and secure place for the working women away from their native place/ homes with all functional facilities like accommodation, food, day-care facility for their children, wherever possible, in urban, semi-urban, or even rural areas where employment opportunities for women exist on nominal cost basis. These are free of cost for users. - Focus: To promote well-being and deliver a package of services to the community. - Funding: It is funded through the National Health Mission (NHM). - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY): - Background: Previously known as the Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS), PM-JAY is the world's largest health insurance scheme. - Beneficiaries: - The beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011). - Also included are families who were part of the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) but were not part of the SECC 2011. - All senior citizens aged 70 years or older. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

Key Features: - Core elements of ABDM: - Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and ABHA app: A 14-digit identification number for access to medical records; an app for uploading/scanning health documents. - Health facility registry: A database of all public and private healthcare facilities. - Registry of healthcare professionals: A comprehensive repository of all healthcare professionals, with availability in both modern and traditional treatment modalities. - Unified Health Interface (UHI): An open platform for appointments, teleconsultations, etc. - Health Information Exchange and Consent Management (HIECM): Allows citizens to securely access and share their health records, ensuring data sharing occurs with the consent of the data holder. - National Health Registry Exchange (HCX): Standardizes and expedites insurance claim processing. - Micro site project: This refers to a group of all healthcare providers, hospitals, pharmacies, etc. It promotes the adoption of ABDM, especially for private sector service providers. - Key initiatives of ABDM: - Scan & Share: Reduces waiting time for OPD registration through QR code-based system.

It is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK): The objective is to provide better healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns, and to address the problem of high out-of-pocket expenditure during childbirth. This program provides the facility of 'free delivery' to pregnant women who use government health facilities for their delivery.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

1.3 SERVICES & ACTIVITIES The scheme will provide financial support for service delivery and for hiring of technical/ other required manpower for the initiatives for immediate and long-term care and support to the targeted women. The services include: - i. Emergency/ Immediate services &short-term care: Putting in place mechanisms for providing a continuum of support and care for women affected by violenceand women in distress through dedicated 24 hours helpline by a national toll-free number and integrated services such as temporary shelter, legal aid, psycho-social counselling, medical assistance, police facilitation and link them with existing services etc. through One Stop Centres. - ii. Institutional Care for long term support: The long-term institutional care component, inter alia, includes taking care of the needs of women right from the conception stage till the time they need such care and support because of their physical, financial and sociological status due to various factors. The support system, inter-alia, includes financial support through direct benefit transfer (DBT) route, shelter, food, rescue & rehabilitation services, counselling, functional literacy, vocational training for skill development, entrepreneurship and linkages with various other support and referral services to destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of violence, and working women or those who do not have anyone to take care through Shakti Sadan , a home for destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of trafficking etc. to provide care and support and all the daily needs and services. SakhiNiwas or Working Women Hostel will provide a safe and secure place for the working women away from their native place/ homes with all functional facilities like accommodation, food, day-care facility for their children, wherever possible, in urban, semi-urban, or even rural areas where employment opportunities for women exist on nominal cost basis. The Palna or National Creche component will provide a safe and secure place for the children of working mothers in the age group of 6 months to 6 years for 7 1/2 hours a day. Financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as for partial compensation of wage loss, if any.

rows.user_input: Please explain what the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan is and how it benefits women and infants.
retrieved_contexts: Interventions: - Sensitizing healthcare providers to provide respectful maternity care, along with close monitoring of their language, behavior, and conduct in the labor room and OT. - Creating a conducive environment for normal/vaginal deliveries. - Ensuring 24-hour availability of essential services, diagnostic services, medicines, and consumables. - Improving the availability of skilled human resources. - The quality improvement in labor rooms and maternity OTs will be evaluated through National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS). - Each facility achieving a score of 70% on NQAS will be designated as a LaQshya compliant facility. - Objective: To provide affordable and quality healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns. - All pregnant women, mothers up to 6 months postpartum, and all sick neonates will receive free healthcare services. - Beneficiaries: All pregnant women, newborns, and breastfeeding mothers. - Free healthcare benefits include: - Iron folic acid supplementation, - Routine immunization for newborns, - Six home visits for newborn care, - Other components of the Antenatal Care (ANC) package, - At least four antenatal checkups, - At least one checkup under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan.

i. Health Department: - Ensuring MCP cards are available and used. - Ensuring timely ANC of pregnant women and vaccination of child - Promote ANC done under the PradhanMantriSurakshitMatritvaAbhiyan (PMSMA) - Promoting institutional delivery, early initiation of breastfeeding, colostrum feeding and exclusive breastfeeding for first six months. - Organizing sensitization and training programs for PMMVY for all concerned staff.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

2.2.8 Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW) The activities under HEW will be implemented upto the Gram Panchayat level and will be facilitated through District level hubs, which will serve as the focal points. These will cover all the GPs/Anganwadi Centres. The hubs will be built upon by leveraging available resources of a variety of schemes/ programs of the government at the district level and will cover the entire country. Services shall be provided at Gram Panchayat level through convergence with frontline workers under various schemes/ Programmes such as Accredited social health activists (ASHAs), Anganwadi workers (AWW), Auxiliary nurse midwife (ANMs), Common Service Centres (CSCs), Women Self Help Groups (SHGs), Banking Correspondents, ShikshaMitra, KrishiVigyanKendras (KVKs), Elected Women Representatives (EWRs), Protection Officers under PWDAV, National Youth Corps (NYC) Volunteers, NyayaMitra, Sakhi - One-Stop Centres (OSCs), Women Helpline, Start-up India, PradhanMantriKaushalVikasYojana (PMKVY), DeenDayalUpadhyayaGrameenKaushalyaYojana -National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DDU-NRLM), National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojna (PMMY), Stand-Up India, MGNREGA, National Rural Health Mission (NRHM), PM Jan AarogyaYojana, RashtriyaSwasthyaBimaYojana (RSBY), Financial literacy/ inclusion, Digital India, SukanyaSamriddhiYojana, MatritvaSahyogYojana (MSY), JananiSurakshaYojana, Swacch Bharat Abhiyan, Mission Poshan 2.0, Mission Vatsalya, PradhanMantriAwasYojana, PradhanMantriUjjwalaYojana, DeenDayalUpadhyaya Gram JyotiYojana (DDUGJY), JalJeevan Mission, and other women centric schemes/programs of the Central/ State government.

Key Features - Beneficiary enrollment: Enrollment will be done through Common Service Centers using a UIDAI-based verification system. - Inclusiveness: The scheme aims to include women; Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, Divyangjans, and marginalized communities like transgenders; and residents of the North Eastern region, island territories, and hilly areas. - Promoting public awareness about social security: This is promoted through schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, Atal Pension Yojana, and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan Dhan Yojana.
rows.reference: The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan aims to provide affordable and quality healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns. Under this initiative, all pregnant women, mothers up to 6 months postpartum, and all sick neonates receive free healthcare services. These benefits include iron folic acid supplementation, routine immunization for newborns, six home visits for newborn care, other components of the Antenatal Care (ANC) package, at least four antenatal checkups, and at least one checkup under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan.

· Background:
- This is based on the principle of "no child left behind."
- Legislative mandates for the scheme:
- The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.
- The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
- Key components:
- Institutional services:
- Child Care Institutions (CCIs): State governments must establish child care institutions in each district or group of districts to provide residential care for children.
- Sanitation and Hygiene Program (SAP): Implemented by states/union territories for CCIs.
- Non-institutional care services for children:
- Sponsorship: Providing financial assistance to vulnerable children living with extended families/biological relatives.
- Foster Care: Providing financial assistance to individuals who provide foster care for a child.
- Adoption: Facilitated through specialized adoption agencies (SAAs).

rows.response: The National Deworming Day aims to reduce the prevalence of soil-transmitted helminths (STH) or intestinal parasitic worms. The target beneficiaries are all children aged 1-19 years, including both school-going and out-of-school children. It is an inter-ministerial initiative involving the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Women and Child Development, and Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation. The National Disease Control Program acts as the nodal agency for conducting STH surveillance. Implementation occurs through schools and Anganwadi centers. Activities include promoting hygiene, sanitation, safe water practices, and awareness about deworming medication (albendazole).

retrieved_contexts: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) - Objective: To improve the quality of maternal and newborn care through competent and confident healthcare providers during the antenatal and postnatal period. - This is an initiative under the National Health Mission (NHM). - It includes pre-natal care training for labor room staff, post-training follow-up and mentoring support, improving accountability of service providers, etc. - This is a tablet-based application that provides ANMs with the facility to update data for beneficiaries within their jurisdiction. - This is a mobile app-based health education service. - It provides timely, accessible, accurate, and relevant messages to pregnant women, new mothers, and their families from the second trimester of pregnancy up to one year after the child's birth regarding pregnancy, childbirth, and childcare. - This is an integrated blood bank information system that connects all blood banks in the state through a single network. - Objective: To provide better healthcare services to central government employees, pensioners, and their dependents. - myCGHS app: Provides CGHS beneficiaries with improved access to electronic health records (EHRs), information, and resources.

Key initiatives under NHM: - Outreach services: Providing support to community health workers, especially in villages, to discuss sensitive issues. - Maternal Health Scheme (MHS): Providing sanitary napkins to adolescent girls living in rural areas. - National Adolescent Health Program: Implemented by MOHFW and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). - RMNCH+A (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health): Aims to improve child survival rates in India and bring their entire lifespan under the scope of the program. - Universal Immunization Program (UIP) - This program is 100% centrally funded. - It was launched in 1985 and is one of the world's largest immunization programs. - Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) - Background: In 2014, the Government of India launched a flagship program called Mission Indradhanush (MI) to improve low immunization coverage. - Subsequently, IMI was launched with the aim of ensuring that no child is left behind in vaccination. - Communicable Disease Control Program

Key Initiatives under NHM: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY): This is a demand promotion and cash transfer scheme to encourage institutional delivery. It is a 100% centrally sponsored scheme. Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK): The objective is to provide better healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns, and to address the problem of high out-of-pocket expenditure during childbirth. This program provides the facility of 'free delivery' to pregnant women who use government health facilities for their delivery.

Key Initiatives under NHM: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK): The objective is to identify and address developmental delays in children from birth, covering 30 selected health services through screening, timely referral, and free treatment. Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK): This program aims to enable adolescents aged 10-19 years to make informed decisions. School health programs are conducted to detect diseases early, especially non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Community-based interventions will be provided by trained community health workers.

Key initiatives under NHM: - Non Communicable Disease Control Programs - National Program for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke (NPCDCS) - National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI) - National Mental Health Program (NMHP) - National Program on Adolescent Health (NPHCE) - National Palliative Care Program (NPPC) - National Programme for Prevention and Control of Deafness (NPPCD) - National Tobacco Control Program (NTCP) - National Program for Prevention and Management of Burns (NPPMBI) - National Oral Health Program (NOHP)

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a demand promotion and cash transfer scheme to encourage institutional delivery. retrieved_contexts: 4. Age of joining and contribution payment by subscribers The minimum age of joining PY is 18 year and maximum is 40 years. The age of exit and start of pension is 60 years. The subscriber's contributions to APY shall be made through the facility of 'auto-debit' of the prescribed contribution amount from the savings bank account of the subscriber in monthly, quarterly or half-yearly frequency. The subscribers are required to contribute the prescribed contribution amount from the age of joining APY till the age of 60 years. The details of age-wise, pension-wise and contribution-frequency-wise prescribed contribution amount and the indicative pension wealth available for the nominee is given in the table at Annex - 1.

5. Exit, withdrawal and pension payment 5.1 On completion of 60 years, the subscriber will get the guaranteed minimum monthly pension, or higher monthly pension, depending on the investment returns. In exceptional circumstances, i.e., in the event of the death of beneficiary or specified illnesses, as mentioned in the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (Exits and Withdrawals under the National Pension System) Regulations, 2015, before the age of 60 years, the accumulated pension wealth till date would be given to the nominee or the subscriber, as the case may be. In case a subscriber, who has availed Government co-contribution under APY, chooses to voluntarily exit APY before the age 60, he shall only be refunded the contributions made by him to APY, along with the net actual interest earned on his contributions (after deducting the account maintenance charges), whereas, the Government co-contribution, and the interest earned on the Government co-contribution, shall not be returned to such subscribers. 5.2 In case a subscriber, who joined on or after 1st October, 2022, is subsequently found to have been an income-tax payer on or before the date of application, the APY account shall be closed and the accumulated pension wealth till date would be given to the subscriber. **** Annex-1 Monthly, Quarterly and Half-yearly prescribed contributions under APY for different minimum guaranteed amount of pension at different entry age and the return of corpus amount to the nominee <!-- image -->

Other objectives: To provide social security to unorganized sector workers in old age. Key features:
- Voluntary and contribution-based pension: The beneficiary must make special contributions until a specified age. The central government contributes an amount equal to the beneficiary's contribution.
- Minimum guaranteed pension: Under this, the beneficiary will receive a minimum guaranteed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month after the age of 60.
- Family pension: In case of death of the beneficiary during the pension period, the spouse of the beneficiary is entitled to receive 50% of the original pension as family pension. The family pension will be available only to the spouse of the beneficiary.
- Compatibility with other schemes: Eligible individuals can participate in both the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) and PM-SYM.
- Enrollment agency: All Common Service Centers (CSCs) across the country are providing facilities for enrollment in this scheme.
- Payment of contributions: If a beneficiary fails to regularly contribute, they have the option to regularize their payments. In this case, the beneficiary must pay the entire outstanding amount along with a fee determined by the government as a penalty.
- Eligibility criteria for enrollment: The individual must have an Aadhaar card and a savings account/Jan Dhan account with IFSC facility.
- Provisions and refunds related to exiting the scheme:

Atal Pension Yojana (APY) - Details of the Scheme 2.2 Upon the death of the subscriber (before the age of 60 years), the spouse of the subscriber has the option to continue contributing to the APY account of the subscriber for the remaining vesting period till the original subscriber would have attained the age of 60 years. The spouse of the subscriber shall then be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriber until the death of the spouse. After the death of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber. The minimum pension is guaranteed by the Government, i.e., if the accumulated corpus based on contributions earns a lower-than-estimated return on investment and is inadequate to provide the minimum guaranteed pension, the Central Government would fund such inadequacy. Alternatively, if the returns on investment are higher, the subscribers would get enhanced pensionary benefits.

2. Benefits of APY - 2.1 APY is a voluntary, periodic contribution-based pension system, under which the subscriber would receive the following benefits: - (i) Central Government guaranteed minimum pension amount: Each subscriber under APY shall receive a Central Government guaranteed minimum pension of Rs. 1000 per month or Rs. 2000 per month or Rs. 3000 per month or Rs. 4000 per month or Rs. 5000 per month, after the age of 60 years until death; - (ii) Central Government guaranteed minimum pension amount to the spouse: After the subscriber's demise, the spouse of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriber until the death of the spouse; - (iii) Return of the pension wealth to the nominee of the subscriber: After the demise of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber.

Other objectives: Promote EV purchases; environmental protection and energy security; promote local manufacturing; etc. - Components: - Demand Aggregation: To increase the demand for electric two-wheelers (e-2Ws), electric three-wheelers (e-3Ws), e-ambulances, e-rickshaws, and new EV categories. - Capital Expenditure Grants: For providing financial assistance to electric buses (e-buses), establishing charging infrastructure, and modernizing testing agencies of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI). - Administrative Assistance: For Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) activities and Project Management Agency (PMA) fees. - Demand Promotion: To directly reduce the upfront cost of electric vehicles for consumers at the time of purchase. - E-Voucher System: An Aadhaar-based e-KYC enabled e-voucher system to avail incentives. - Sustainability and Safety: - All eligible electric vehicles must meet prescribed safety standards. - Promotes the use of advanced batteries and phasing out of older vehicles. - Implementation of EMPS 2024: Implemented for a period of 6 months from April 1, 2024 to September 30, 2024. retrieved_contexts: Key Features - Other priority sectors (up to 30% of the PMKKKY fund can be used): Infrastructure; irrigation; energy and water conservation; any other measures to improve environmental quality in mining-affected areas. - Distribution of funds in directly and indirectly affected areas: At least 70% of the DMF fund will be spent in the directly affected area. - Endowment fund: This fund should be used to create sustainable livelihoods in areas where mining activities have ceased due to depletion or other reasons. - A maximum of 10% of the annual collections for districts with an annual collection of ₹10 crore or more should be kept as an endowment fund. - The endowment fund can be invested in government securities/bonds, fixed deposits in scheduled banks, and other places approved by the state government. - Project Management Units (PMUs): DMFs with an annual collection of over ₹50 crore will have to establish a PMU for planning and providing technical, accounting, and monitoring support. - Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): All funds will be transferred directly to the bank accounts of implementing agencies and beneficiaries through DBT.

Key Features - District Mineral Foundation (DMF): The DMF is essentially a non-profit trust established by state governments in all mining-affected districts under the MMDR Act, 1957. - Chairman of the Governing Council and Managing Committee: The District Magistrate/ Deputy Commissioner/ Collector of the district. - Existing mining companies are required to contribute 30% of the royalty, and companies that acquire mines through auction are required to contribute 10% of the royalty (based on the date of the granted mining lease). This is separate from the royalty paid by mining companies to state governments. - Affected area: The responsibility has been entrusted to the DMF to prepare and maintain a list of areas affected by mining activities. - Directly affected area: The state government can declare an area within 15 km of the mine(s) (excluding small mines) as a directly affected area. - Indirectly affected area: The state government can declare an area beyond that distance (not more than 25 km) from the mine(s) (excluding small mines) as an indirectly affected area, even if it does not fall within the boundaries of the concerned district or the adjacent district.

Key Points - Objective of the plan: To ensure that all District Mineral Foundations (DMFs) provide certain minimum provisions for development programs. - Legal recognition: The central government launched this scheme in 2015 under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (MMDR Act). - Beneficiaries: Directly affected people and directly or indirectly affected areas. - Accountability: Annual audits of DMF accounts are conducted.

Coordination with other schemes in PMKKKY - The DMF will focus on coordinating with existing central and state schemes to achieve sustainable development goals in mining-affected areas. - Efforts will be made to coordinate with state and district plans so that the activities undertaken by the DMF can complement welfare activities and be considered as an additional budgetary resource for the state plan. - Priority should be given to achieving the targets set under the Aspirational Districts Program and the Aspirational Blocks Program. - Activities carried out under the 'Polluter Pays' principle are not eligible under PMKKKY. - Baseline survey: A baseline survey will be conducted by districts for perspective planning. Gram Sabhas/local bodies can assist in preparing a local evaluation report. - Five-year perspective plan: Based on the data obtained through the baseline survey or any other survey/evaluation, and based on the identified priorities, the DMF will prepare a strategic plan for five years and include it in the perspective plan. - Annual plans: The annual plans of the DMF will be based on the five-year perspective plan and the success achieved in achieving its goals in previous years.

Key Features - Background: This scheme was launched under the MSME Champions Scheme in 2022. It incorporates the following schemes: - Pradhan Mantri Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) - Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) - Scope of assistance: - Assistance is available only for new units being established. - Applicable to all micro enterprises (technically and economically) in rural and urban areas. - No income limit for projects being set up. - Only one member of the family is eligible to receive financial assistance. - Digitalization: Online processing of applications directly by financing branches and allocation of margin money. - Priority beneficiaries and banks: - Applicants from aspirational districts and transgender persons will be included in the priority category to avail assistance. - Maximum project cost: - 50 lakhs for the manufacturing sector and 20 lakhs for the service sector. - The remaining project cost will be provided by banks as term loans.
rows.response: Project Management Units (PMUs) are required for District Mineral Foundations (DMFs) with an annual collection of over ₹50 crore to provide planning, technical, accounting, and monitoring support.
rows.reference: Districts with an annual collection of over ₹50 crore must establish a Project Management Unit (PMU) to provide planning and technical, accounting, and monitoring support.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

1.1 VISION AND MISSION These guidelines have been developed to support stakeholders and agencies who would be involved in implementing the Scheme, as well as State, district and grassroots level functionaries. It is intended to serve as a reference manual for officials at the National, State/Union Territory (UT) and District / grass root levels for policy guidance and monitoring. These guidelines list out the services to be provided under the Scheme and steps and processes/procedures for implementation. These guidelines also highlight the roles and responsibilities of various line departments. It provides indicative monitoring and reporting formats to be used at different levels. The guidelines may be modified based on the feedback received from States/UTs from time to time, as per requirements, to ensure proper implementation.

3.2.2 STATE LEVEL The overall implementation of the Scheme at State/UT level will be done by a Committee headed by the Chief Secretary. The committee will be serviced by the Department of Women and Child Development/ Social Welfare Department of concerned States/ UTs. The other members of the Committee would be nominated by the Chief Secretary drawing officers from relevant departments like education, health, police, skill development, Banks/ FIs etc on the same line as the National Level Committee. The Committee shall meet at least twice a year and monitor the projects/ schemes. The Committee will also prepare the Annual Action Plan for the State under various components of the Scheme. Continuation of grant to any agency would depend on the satisfactory performance as assessed by the State/ UT level Committee.

4.2 REPORTING Standardized monitoring reports, covering both financial as well as operational performance data will be prepared for the scheme by the State Level/District Level Monitoring Committee, as the case may be, on a quarterly basis and sent to the Central Government that will review the reports on a quarterly basis. A comprehensive web-based reporting system will be developed and put in place to enable real-time monitoring. The web-enabled monitoring system would be a user-friendly single portal providing Management Information System (MIS) and easy accessibility while giving due regard to maintaining the confidentiality of data. It will enable monitoring of the program including inter alia establishment of service delivery structures; accurate information about the network of institutions available, services being provided, human resources, financial resources and beneficiaries. In addition, the portal would also showcase updated data on vulnerable categories of women as well as those already in need of care and support; as well as information on the impact of services and of campaigns for thought and behavior change. The evaluation of the scheme would be assessed by a third party of repute to be nominated by MWCD.

rows.user_input: Under the DAY-NRLM scheme, which families are categorized as Priority One (POP) based on the socioeconomic caste census?
retrieved_contexts: Key Features: - Identification of beneficiaries: - All rural poor families listed in the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC), 2011, with at least one deprivation. - Participatory Mapping Process (PIP): During village visits, community functionaries will conduct PIP activities (e.g., social mapping, ranking/grouping based on wealth and welfare, vulnerability assessment, door-to-door surveys of the poorest villages). - Families included in DAY-NRLM will be listed as "Priority One" (POP) in the PIP. This list will be approved by the Gram Panchayat.

Key Initiatives under DAY-NRLM: - Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushal Yojana (DDU-GKY): An inclusive program for rural youth aged 15-35, and individuals with disabilities, with a reservation of 50% for Scheduled Castes/Tribes, 15% for minorities, and 33% for women. - "From Support to Prosperity - Leaving No Rural Woman Behind": This campaign aims to connect 10 crore rural women as part of the Amrit Mahotsav inclusive skill development initiative.

Key Initiatives under DAY-NRLM: - Skill Development Program (ASDP): 25% of NRLM funds are allocated to ASDP. It helps rural youth acquire skills and find suitable, well-paying jobs in growing sectors of the economy. - Mahalaxmi Krishi Sahayak Pariyojana (MKSP): Increases women's participation and productivity in agriculture and allied activities. - National Rural Livelihoods Project (NRLP): A World Bank-approved project of $500 million in 2011. - National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP): Promotes digital assets and livelihood initiatives. Funded by the World Bank. - Saksham Centres: Objective: To provide financial literacy to SHG members and rural poor, and facilitate access to financial services (savings, loans, insurance, pensions, etc.). - Aajeevika Gramin Employment Yojana (AGEY): AGEY aims to connect rural areas through vehicles owned by Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

Key Features: - Background: The PMAY-G aimed to construct 2.95 crore basic facilities by March 2024. - Now, this scheme has been extended to include remaining eligible families in the Housing+ (2018) list (after operation) and the SECC 2011 Permanent Waiting List (PWL). - Selection of Beneficiaries: - The Housing+ is designed to obtain relevant information about eligible families, including a current photograph of their housing and the location where the PMAY-G house will be constructed. - A three-stage verification process (Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011, Gram Sabha, and Geo-tagging). - Prioritization of beneficiaries: Priority will be determined based on criteria for families with housing in each category, namely Scheduled Castes/Tribes and others. - In accordance with the "Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016", states may ensure that up to 5% of the beneficiaries at the state level are persons with disabilities, and priority is given to women with disabilities. - Verification of prioritization lists by the Gram Sabha or relevant local self-governance unit.

Key Features: - Background: Initiated based on the recommendation of the National Health Policy, 2017. - Benefits: See infographic at the end. - Ayushman Arogya Mandir (formerly Health and Wellness Centers): - 1,50,000 Health and Wellness Centers (HWCs) will be created to provide comprehensive primary healthcare (CPHC). These are free of cost for users. - Focus: To promote well-being and deliver a package of services to the community. - Funding: It is funded through the National Health Mission (NHM). - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY): - Background: Previously known as the Rashtriya Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (NHPS), PM-JAY is the world's largest health insurance scheme. - Beneficiaries: - The beneficiaries are identified through the Socio-Economic Caste Census 2011 (SECC 2011). - Also included are families who were part of the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) but were not part of the SECC 2011. - All senior citizens aged 70 years or older. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

rows.user_input: What specific roles do "Nari Adalats" (women's courts) play in addressing women's grievances at the state/union territory level, and how are "Palna" daycare facilities managed?
retrieved_contexts: 2.1.4 Nari Adalat Nari Adalat a new component for providing women with an alternate Grievance Redressal Mechanism for resolving cases of petty nature (harassment, subversion, curtailment of rights or entitlements) faced by women at Gram Panachayat level will be implemented in a phased manner. Nari Adalats or women collectives will be formed of committed and socially respected women chosen for that purpose. This platform will also be utilized for engaging with the public for awareness generation and getting feedback for improvement in the schemes and for effective public delivery of services. These will be provided logistic support through Gram Panchayats in convergence with the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, and Common Service Centres (CSCs) run by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. Initially, it will be launched in identified States/UTs, preferably where Elected Women Representatives (EWRs) are heading the Gram Panchayats (GPs) in Aspirational Districts. In the first year, an awareness drive regarding legal, constitutional rights and entitlements under various schemes/ programs will be undertaken. In the second year, committed and socially respected women will be identified and extensively trained in all women-related laws and schemes and a formal setup of women collectives having 7 to 11 members will be made who will address the socio, economic, and cultural issues faced by the women of that area and will provide alternative resolution to disputes by mediation and by connecting them to the duty bearers. Under this component, no remuneration to the selected members shall be provided. However, out-of-pocket expenses will be provided by the Ministry for organising the meetings and for providing the badge/ uniform to the members.

2.2.5Palna - Crechefacility The Government's sustained initiative on education and employment of women has resulted in increased opportunities for their employment, and more and more women are now in gainful employment, working within or outside their homes. The growing industrialization and urban development have led to increased migration into the cities. The past few decades have shown a rapid increase in nuclear families. Thus, the children of such working women, who were earlier getting support from families while they were at work, are now in need of day care services which provide quality care and protection for the children. Children who used to grow up in the secure and warm laps of their grandmothers and other family members are now confronted with an insecure and neglected environment; therefore, women need a safe place for their children in their absence. It has become necessary to provide support to the young children in terms of quality care and other services while the mothers are at work. Effective day care for young children is essential and a cost-effective investment as it provides support to both mothers and young children. Lack of proper day-care services is, often, a deterrent for women to go out and work. Hence, there is an urgent need for improved quality and reach of day care services/crèches for working women amongst all socioeconomic groups both in the organized and unorganized sectors. Considering the difficulties faced by the working mothers in giving due child care and protection to their children, it has been decided to provide the day-care crèche facilities through the component of Palna. Creche services formalize the child care facilities hitherto considered as part of domestic work. Formalization of care work supports 'decent work campaign' to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal 8 - Decentwork and economic growth.

2.2.4 Component for Working Women Another objective of the SakhiNiwas component under the sub-scheme is to promote availability of safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women, with day care facilities for women living in hostels. The Day care/ Palna facility will also be open for the children of other working women living in the vicinity, subject to availability of slots, wherever possible. The working women's hostel projects under this scheme shall be made available to all working women without any distinction with respect to caste, religion, marital status etc., subject to norms prescribed under the scheme. The facility of ShakhiNiwas can be availed by any working women, who may be single, widowed, divorced, separated or married (whose immediate family does not reside in the same city/area). Preference will be given to women from disadvantaged sections of the society. Special preference would be given to beneficiaries with physical disabilities, in case there is shortage of accommodation. Women who are under training for a job will also be considered for accommodation subject to availability and provided that the total training period does not exceed one year. The number of women under training for jobs should not exceed 30% of the total capacity. Girls up to the age of 18 years and boys up to the age of 12 years, accompanying working mothers will be provided accommodation with their mothers. Working mothers may also avail of the services of the Day Care Centre, as provided under the scheme. The gross income of the beneficiaries should not exceed Rs. 50,000/- consolidated (gross) per month in metropolitan cities, and Rs 35,000/-consolidated (gross) per month, in any other place. The income ceiling can be relaxed by District Magistrate or any other authorised officer based on the local requirement and subject to availability of accommodation. When the income of any working woman already residing in a hostel exceeds the prescribed limits, she will be required to vacate the hostel within a period of six months of crossing the income ceiling.

1.3 SERVICES & ACTIVITIES The scheme will provide financial support for service delivery and for hiring of technical/ other required manpower for the initiatives for immediate and long-term care and support to the targeted women. The services include: - i. Emergency/ Immediate services &short-term care: Putting in place mechanisms for providing a continuum of support and care for women affected by violenceand women in distress through dedicated 24 hours helpline by a national toll-free number and integrated services such as temporary shelter, legal aid, psycho-social counselling, medical assistance, police facilitation and link them with existing services etc. through One Stop Centres. - ii. Institutional Care for long term support: The long-term institutional care component, inter alia, includes taking care of the needs of women right from the conception stage till the time they need such care and support because of their physical, financial and sociological status due to various factors. The support system, inter-alia, includes financial support through direct benefit transfer (DBT) route, shelter, food, rescue & rehabilitation services, counselling, functional literacy, vocational training for skill development, entrepreneurship and linkages with various other support and referral services to destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of violence, and working women or those who do not have anyone to take care through Shakti Sadan , a home for destitute, distressed, marginalized, victims of trafficking etc. to provide care and support and all the daily needs and services. SakhiNiwas or Working Women Hostel will provide a safe and secure place for the working women away from their native place/ homes with all functional facilities like accommodation, food, day-care facility for their children, wherever possible, in urban, semi-urban, or even rural areas where employment opportunities for women exist on nominal cost basis. The Palna or National Creche component will provide a safe and secure place for the children of working mothers in the age group of 6 months to 6 years for 7 1/2 hours a day. Financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as for partial compensation of wage loss, if any.

2.2.5Palna - Crechefacility The objective of the Palna component of the sub-scheme is to address the urgent need for quality crèche care facilities by providing a safe & secure environment for nutritional, health and cognitive development of the children, thereby enabling more mothers to take up gainful employment. The objective to provide crèche facility to all mothers, irrespective of their employment status, is a marked shift from the existing policy, arising out of the understanding that existence of quality crèche facilities is a necessary precondition to encourage women to explore employment opportunities. Apart from the aforementioned primary objective, another objective of the component would involve monitoring compliance of the stipulations laid down in Section 11A of the Maternity Benefit Act regarding setting up of crèche facilities by the establishments. For this purpose, the States/UTs would explore the possibility of hosting an application/portal in convergence with the Labour & Employment Departments of their respective States/UTs for facilitating establishments to register on the portal and furnish details in respect of the crèches set up in accordance with the Act. It is also envisaged to include provisions in the portal to enable employees to report non-compliance by establishments for taking penal action in accordance with the provisions stipulated under Section 21 of the Maternity Benefit Act. Under the component, an integrated package of services such as day care facilities including Sleeping Facilities, Early Stimulation for children below 3 years and Pre-school Education for 3 to 6 years old children, Supplementary Nutrition (to be locally sourced), Growth Monitoring and Health Check-up and Immunization in convergence with Mission
rows.reference: In the context of Nari Adalat, the initiative will be initially launched in identified States/UTs, preferably where Elected Women Representatives (EWRs) head Gram Panchayats in Aspirational Districts. This platform provides an alternative Grievance Redressal Mechanism for women facing issues like harassment or curtailment of rights at the Gram Panchayat level. Regarding the Palna component, States/UTs are expected to explore the possibility of hosting an application or portal in convergence with their respective Labour & Employment Departments. This portal will facilitate establishments to register and provide details regarding crèche facilities set up in accordance with the Maternity Benefit Act, while also allowing employees to report non-compliance for potential penal action.

rows.user_input: As a community worker, can you explain how the integration of e-Sanjivani with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission helps mothers in our village, particularly by facilitating their Ayushman Bharat Health Account?
retrieved_contexts: e-Sanjivani LaQshya Labor Room Quality Improvement Initiative - This is a national telemedicine service that aims to provide traditional physical consultations through a digital platform. - The National Health Authority (NHA) has announced the successful integration of e-Sanjivani with ABDM (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission). - This integration enables existing e-Sanjivani users to easily create their Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and link it to their existing health records. - Objective: To reduce preventable maternal and neonatal mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with care during labor and delivery, and to provide respectful maternity care.

Key Features: - Core elements of ABDM: - Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and ABHA app: A 14-digit identification number for access to medical records; an app for uploading/scanning health documents. - Health facility registry: A database of all public and private healthcare facilities. - Registry of healthcare professionals: A comprehensive repository of all healthcare professionals, with availability in both modern and traditional treatment modalities. - Unified Health Interface (UHI): An open platform for appointments, teleconsultations, etc. - Health Information Exchange and Consent Management (HIECM): Allows citizens to securely access and share their health records, ensuring data sharing occurs with the consent of the data holder. - National Health Registry Exchange (HCX): Standardizes and expedites insurance claim processing. - Micro site project: This refers to a group of all healthcare providers, hospitals, pharmacies, etc. It promotes the adoption of ABDM, especially for private sector service providers. - Key initiatives of ABDM: - Scan & Share: Reduces waiting time for OPD registration through QR code-based system.

Key Features: - Ayushman Bhava Abhiyan: To expand comprehensive healthcare coverage to every village and town, overcoming geographical barriers. It aims to ensure that no one is left behind. The objective is to improve the reach of health services through three components: - Ayushman - Aapke Dwar 3.0, - Ayushman Arogya Mandir and community health centers (CHCs) with Ayushman fairs, and - Ayushman Sabha in every village and panchayat.

2.2.1 Shakti Sadan The residents of Shakti Sadan will be provided with shelter, food, clothing, primary health facilities and other essential daily need items. Residents will be facilitated for opening Bank Accounts in their names in which an amount of Rs. 500 per month per resident shall be deposited, which cannot be withdrawn by the account holders during their stay in the home. However, if the resident is willing to avail the benefits for PM JeewanJyotiBimaYojana and/ or PM SurakshaBimaYojana, payment of premium can be made out of the aforementioned amount. The amount deposited along with accrued interest can be utilised as seed money by the beneficiary for beginning her life/ career afresh after she leaves the home. Vocational training and social security benefits (including medical benefit under Ayushman Bharat Yojana or similar schemes, Disability Pension) etc. shall be arranged for the residents of homes in convergence with the relevant departments. Their special needs, if any, will also be taken care of. For other services like psycho-social counselling, legal aid, there shall be a common pool of persons under overall charge of OSC.

ii. Panchayati Raj Institutions: - Organizing community awareness events. - Providing additional incentives to mothers through their own funds. - Conducting social audits/addressing grievances. - Ensuring registration of Child Birth - iii. UIDAI: The beneficiaries without Aadhaar may be provided Aadhaar number. - iv. Information / Public Relations Department: Publicity and mass reach through - All India  Radio,  Song  and  Drama  Division,  Directorate  of  Advertising  and  Visual Publicity  (DAVP),  Division  of  Field  Publicity,  State  IEC  Bureau,  Print  Media, Regional TV channels, social media etc. - v. Lead  State  and  District  Post  Office/Banks: For  opening  of  JAM  Account  (JanDhan accounts seeded with Aadhaar and Mobile number) for PMMVY beneficiaries and devising appropriate cash transfer mechanism for smooth transactions in all the districts. - vi. State  Training  Institutes/Medical  Colleges for  ensuring  their  training  curriculum includes training on the PMMVY.
rows.reference: The integration of e-Sanjivani with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) allows existing e-Sanjivani users to easily create their Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) and link it to their existing health records. This initiative is part of the LaQshya Labor Room Quality Improvement Initiative, which aims to provide respectful maternity care while reducing preventable maternal and neonatal mortality, morbidity, and stillbirths associated with care during labor and delivery.

rows.user_input: How does the incentive structure for the production of Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) relate to the FAME-II scheme concerning electric vehicle incentives?
retrieved_contexts: Key Features - About Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC): ACCs are next-generation energy storage technologies. - They can store electrical energy in the form of electrochemical or chemical energy and convert it back into electrical energy when needed. - Objective: To achieve a manufacturing capacity of 50 GWh of ACCs and an additional cumulative capacity of 5 GW for related ACC technologies. - Incentive: The total annual cash incentive provided by the government will be up to ₹20,000 crore per beneficiary firm. - The beneficiary firm must commit to setting up a minimum of 5 GW of ACC manufacturing facilities. - Technology Agnostic: The beneficiary firm will have the freedom to choose advanced technologies and related plant & machinery, raw materials, and other intermediary goods. - Exclusion: The conventional battery pack segment of the industry will not be incentivized, even though its production already exists in India. - Impact on Other Schemes: Any claim for incentives under this scheme will not nullify/invalidate any claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

Key Features - Distinction from FAME-II: The incentives provided under this scheme for electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers will be independent of the incentives offered for electric (and hybrid) vehicles under the FAME/FAME II scheme. - Project Implementation Agency (PIA): National Productivity Council (NPC) is the Project Implementation Agency. NPC is a non-profit organization that promotes productivity and competitiveness in Indian industries.

Important Points - Scope of the Scheme: This is a centrally sponsored scheme. - Objective of the Scheme: To enhance India's advanced chemistry cell (ACC) battery storage manufacturing capabilities. - Localization: Minimum 25% domestic value addition at the 'mother unit level' and 60% at the 'cell level'. - Monitoring: Monitored by a Group of Secretaries (EGoS) chaired by the Cabinet Secretary. Other objectives: To achieve higher domestic value addition. Also, to ensure that the cost of battery manufacturing in India is competitive on a global scale.

Key Features - Background: India has the potential to become the world's third largest automotive market by volume by 2026. - Incentives: - An incentive of up to 18% for new investments in the indigenous supply chain of advanced automotive technology (AAT). - A total incentive of approximately ₹6,485 crore for eligible companies/groups of companies. - It follows a phased manufacturing program adopted under the FAME-II scheme. - Base year for calculating eligible turnover: 2019-20. - The incentive is available from 2023-24 for a continuous period of five financial years, i.e., up to the financial year 2027-28. Previously, this incentive was available up to the financial year 2026-27. - Conditions for availing incentives: - This scheme includes two components: - Eligibility: Both existing and new manufacturing companies that meet revenue (from automotive and/or auto component manufacturing) and investment (company or its group's global investment in fixed assets) criteria.

Key Features: - Objective: To accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), promote charging infrastructure, and boost EV manufacturing facilities. - Type: Centrally sponsored scheme. - Duration: October 2024 to March 31, 2026. - Goal: To incentivize the adoption of electric two-wheelers (e-2Ws), electric three-wheelers (e-3Ws), e-ambulances, e-rickshaws, and e-buses. Other objectives: Promote EV purchases; environmental protection and energy security; promote local manufacturing; etc. - Components: - Demand Aggregation: To increase the demand for electric two-wheelers (e-2Ws), electric three-wheelers (e-3Ws), e-ambulances, e-rickshaws, and new EV categories. - Capital Expenditure Grants: For providing financial assistance to electric buses (e-buses), establishing charging infrastructure, and modernizing testing agencies of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI). - Administrative Assistance: For Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) activities and Project Management Agency (PMA) fees. - Demand Promotion: To directly reduce the upfront cost of electric vehicles for consumers at the time of purchase. - E-Voucher System: An Aadhaar-based e-KYC enabled e-voucher system to avail incentives. - Sustainability and Safety: - All eligible electric vehicles must meet prescribed safety standards. - Promotes the use of advanced batteries and phasing out of older vehicles. - Implementation of EMPS 2024: Implemented for a period of 6 months from April 1, 2024 to September 30, 2024. Subsequently, it was included in the PM E-DRIVE scheme.
rows.response: The incentives provided for electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers under the Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) scheme are independent of those offered for electric (and hybrid) vehicles under the FAME/FAME II scheme. Additionally, any claim for incentives under this scheme will not nullify or invalidate any claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

Furthermore, any claim for incentives under the ACC scheme will not nullify or invalidate any claims made for automobiles and auto components under the FAME-II or PLI schemes.

rows.user_input: What functions are performed by urban local bodies for rural areas, and how do they assist in initiatives like solar energy to help villages become self-reliant in terms of electricity?
retrieved_contexts: Important Points: - Objective of the scheme: To promote the installation of solar rooftop panels and make residential areas self-sufficient in electricity generation. - Model Solar Villages: In each district, a village will be designated as a "model solar village" to encourage the adoption of rooftop solar systems (RTS) in rural areas. - Incentives for local bodies: Urban local bodies and panchayat raj institutions will be encouraged to promote the installation of RTS in their areas. - Duration: 2024 to 2026-27

Key Features - Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation: Emergency Response Units (ERSUs) located in the largest urban local bodies in each district will provide emergency sanitation services in peripheral areas, i.e., rural areas. - Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship: To provide vocational training to SSWs in coordination with PMKVY. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> - Responsibilities of Urban Local Bodies - To create a database by tagging sewers and septic tanks. - To maintain sewer lines regularly to avoid the need for emergency cleaning. - To identify the most suitable technical solution for the city/town. - Septage treatment systems, including sludge digestion plants, will be established in areas with septic tanks. - Local authorities will standardize the design of septic tanks and ensure its adoption. - Implementation Agency: - IEC Campaign: This campaign is run by ULBs and NSKFDC and will make extensive use of social media. - Monitoring: A multi-level working group will be constituted at central, state, and district levels to monitor the implementation of this scheme. <!-- image -->

Key Initiatives under PM JANMAN - New Solar Energy Scheme for PVTG Communities/Villages: For electrification of 1 lakh unelectrified households (HHs) in PVTG areas. This includes: - Solar Home Lighting System (SHLS): For unelectrified households (HHs) in remote PVTG areas. The installation of LED bulbs and fans along with on-site maintenance services for 5 years will be free of cost. - Solar Grid: For a group of HHs. The Ministry will provide a limited CFA assistance of ₹50,000 per HH covered under the grid scheme. - Solarization of Multi-Purpose Centers (MPCs): In PVTG areas where electricity is not available through the grid. Off-grid solar power packs with battery banks will be installed. The Ministry will provide a limited CFA assistance of up to ₹1 lakh per MPC. - IEC Campaign for PM JANMAN: To raise awareness among tribal families and ensure 100% access to government schemes.

After the death of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber. The minimum pension is guaranteed by the Government, i.e., if the accumulated corpus based on contributions earns a lower-than-estimated return on investment and is inadequate to provide the minimum guaranteed pension, the Central Government would fund such inadequacy. Alternatively, if the returns on investment are higher, the subscribers would get enhanced pensionary benefits.
rows.reference: In case a subscriber who has availed Government co-contribution under APY chooses to voluntarily exit APY before the age of 60, he shall only be refunded the contributions made by him to APY, along with the net actual interest earned on his contributions (after deducting the account maintenance charges). The Government co-contribution and the interest earned on the Government co-contribution shall not be returned to such subscribers.

retrieved_contexts: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) -  The act was notified in 2005 , all the rural areas have been covered since 2008 -  Main aim is improve the livelihood security of rural household -  A right based act i.e providing unskilled manual work to those who demand it -  Who can demand work? : any adult member of a rural household who is ready to do unskilled manual work -  How many days of work? : upto 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in  a financial year ( April1st to March 31st). The days can be increased by the central govt. or the state govt. concerned. -  How is it guaranteed : providing work within 15 days of the demand for work or else unemployment allowance has to be given. Implementation of Act -  PRI to be responsible for planning, monitoring and implementation of the work. -  Gram sabha to recommend works which will be executed by the panchayat.

i. Health Department: - Ensuring MCP cards are available and used. - Ensuring timely ANC of pregnant women and vaccination of child - Promote ANC done under the PradhanMantriSurakshitMatritvaAbhiyan (PMSMA) - Promoting institutional delivery, early initiation of breastfeeding, colostrum feeding and exclusive breastfeeding for first six months. - Organizing sensitization and training programs for PMMVY for all concerned staff.

2.2.6Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) The Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) with effect from 1 st January 2017. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card

Key initiatives under NHM: - Outreach services: Providing support to community health workers, especially in villages, to discuss sensitive issues. - Maternal Health Scheme (MHS): Providing sanitary napkins to adolescent girls living in rural areas. - National Adolescent Health Program: Implemented by MOHFW and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). - RMNCH+A (Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health): Aims to improve child survival rates in India and bring their entire lifespan under the scope of the program. - Universal Immunization Program (UIP) - This program is 100% centrally funded. - It was launched in 1985 and is one of the world's largest immunization programs. - Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) - Background: In 2014, the Government of India launched a flagship program called Mission Indradhanush (MI) to improve low immunization coverage. - Subsequently, IMI was launched with the aim of ensuring that no child is left behind in vaccination. - Communicable Disease Control Program

Key initiatives under NHM: - National Vector Borne Disease Control Program (NVBDCP): Launched to prevent and control vector-borne diseases such as malaria, Japanese encephalitis, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, and visceral filariasis. - National Tuberculosis Elimination Program (NTEP): Aims to reduce the number of TB cases in India by 2025, five years ahead of the Sustainable Development Goals. - Nikshay Poshan Yojana (NPY): Provides financial assistance of ₹1000 per month to TB patients through DBT. - National Leprosy Eradication Program (NLEP): Provides quality leprosy services free of charge to all sections of the population. - Integrated Disease Surveillance Program (IDSP): Aims to strengthen a centralized, district-based information technology-enabled disease surveillance system for epidemic-prone diseases.

· Background:

- Institutional services:

rows.response: The National Deworming Day aims to reduce the prevalence of soil-transmitted helminths (STH) or intestinal parasitic worms. The program targets all children aged 1-19 years, including both school-going and out-of-school children. It is an inter-ministerial initiative involving the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Women and Child Development, and Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation. The National Disease Control Program acts as the nodal agency for conducting STH surveillance. Implementation occurs through schools and Anganwadi centers. Activities include promoting hygiene, sanitation, safe water practices, and generating awareness about deworming medication (albendazole).

This inter-ministerial initiative involves the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, and the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation. Implementation occurs through schools and Anganwadi centers. Activities include promoting hygiene, sanitation, and safe water practices, as well as generating awareness about deworming medication (albendazole).

The spouse of the subscriber shall then be entitled to receive the same pension amount as that of the subscriber until the death of the spouse. After the death of both, the subscriber and the spouse, the nominee of the subscriber shall be entitled to receive the pension wealth, as accumulated till the age of 60 years of the subscriber. The PMMVY Scheme is being implemented as per provisions under Section 4 of the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 which provides for financial support for pregnant and lactating mothers is to improve the health and nutrition for mother and child as well as compensation for wage loss, if any. The Objectives of the PMMVYis to provide cash incentive for partial compensation for the wage loss so that the woman can take adequate rest before and after delivery of the first child; and to improve health seeking behaviour amongst the Pregnant Women & Lactating Mothers (PW&LM). The scheme also seeks to promote positive behavioural change towards girl child by providing additional cash incentive for the second child, if that is a girl child. Under this component free of charge meal, during pregnancy and six months after the childbirth, through the local Anganwadi is envisaged so as to meet the nutritional standards; and maternity benefit of not less than rupees five thousand, in two instalments will be provided to women belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society. However, any additional incentive available under any other scheme such as JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) shall continue to be availed. The eligible beneficiaries would receive the remaining cash incentives as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an average, a woman will get ₹ 6000/- . The criteria for determining socially and economically disadvantaged sections of society will be the following: - i. Women belonging to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes; - ii. Women who are partially (40%) or fully disabled (Divyang Jan) - iii. Women holder of BPL ration Card
rows.reference: Under the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, the objective is to provide affordable and quality healthcare services to pregnant women and newborns.
